AS-2.2.9.text: Guards of elephant forests, assisted by those who rear elephants, those who enchain the legs of elephants, those who guard the boundaries, those who live in forests, as well as by those who nurse elephants, shall, with the help of five or seven female elephants to help in tethering wild ones, trace the whereabouts of herds of elephants by following the course of urine and dungs left by elephants and along forest-tracts covered over with branches of Bhallátaki (Semicarpus Anacardium), and by observing the spots where elephants slept or sat before or left dungs, or where they had just destroyed the banks of rivers or lakes.
AS-2.2.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 2, Sutra 9 (AS-2.2.9)

AS-2.20.1.text: THE Superintendent of lineal measure shall possess the knowledge of measuring space and time. 8 atoms (paramánavah) are equal to 1 particle thrown off by the wheel of a chariot. 8 particles are equal to 1 likshá. 8 likshás are equal to the middle of a yúka (louse) or a yúka of medium size. 8 yúkas are equal to 1 yava (barley) of middle size. 8 yavas are equal to
AS-2.20.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 1 (AS-2.20.1)

AS-2.20.10.text: Likewise when the day declines, the same process in reverse order shall be observed.
AS-2.20.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 10 (AS-2.20.10)

AS-2.20.11.text: It is in the month of Ashádha that no shadow is cast in midday. After Ashádha, during the six months from Srávana upwards, the length of shadow successively increases by two angulas and during the next six months from Mágha upwards, it successively decreases by two angulas.
AS-2.20.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 11 (AS-2.20.11)

AS-2.20.12.text: Fifteen days and nights together make up one paksha. That paksha during which the moon waxes is white (sukla) and that paksha during which the moon wanes is bahula.
AS-2.20.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 12 (AS-2.20.12)

AS-2.20.13.text: Two pakshas make one month (mása). Thirty days and nights together make one work-a-month (prakarmamásah). The same (30 days and nights) with an additional half a day makes one solar month (saura).
AS-2.20.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 13 (AS-2.20.13)

AS-2.20.14.text: The same (30) less by half a day makes one lunar month (chandramása).
AS-2.20.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 14 (AS-2.20.14)

AS-2.20.15.text: Twenty-seven (days and nights) make a sidereal month (nakshatramása).
AS-2.20.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 15 (AS-2.20.15)

AS-2.20.16.text: Once in thirty-two months there comes one malamása profane month, i.e., an extra month added to lunar year to harmonise it with the solar.
AS-2.20.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 16 (AS-2.20.16)

AS-2.20.17.text: Once in thirty-five months there comes a malamása for Asvaváhas.
AS-2.20.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 17 (AS-2.20.17)

AS-2.20.18.text: Seasons from sisira and upwards are the summer-solstice (uttaráyana), and (those) from varshá and upwards are the winter solstice (dakshináyana). Two solstices (ayanas) make one year (samvatsara). Five years make one yuga.
AS-2.20.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 18 (AS-2.20.18)

AS-2.20.19.text: The sun carries off (harati) 1/60th of a whole day every day and thus makes one complete day in every two months (ritau). Likewise the moon (falls behind by 1/60th of a whole day every day and falls behind one day in every two months). Thus in the middle of every third year, they (the sun and the moon) make one adhimása, additional month, first in the summer season and second at the end of five years.
AS-2.20.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 19 (AS-2.20.19)

AS-2.20.2.text: 1 angula (¾ of an English inch) or the middlemost joint of the middle finger of a man of medium size may be taken to be equal to an angula. 4 angulas are equal to 1 dhanurgraha. 8 angulas are equal to 1 dhanurmushti. 12 angulas are equal to 1 vitasti, or 1 chháyápaurusha. 14 angulas are equal to 1 sama, sala, pariraya, or pada. 2 vitastis are equal to 1 aratni or 1 prájápatya hasta 2 vitastis plus 1 dhanurgraha are equal to 1 hasta used in measuring balances and cubic measures, and pasture lands. 2 vitastis plus 1 dhanurmusti 1 kishku or 1 kamsa. 42 angulas are equal to
AS-2.20.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 2 (AS-2.20.2)

AS-2.20.3.text: 1 kishku according to sawyers and blacksmiths and used in measuring the grounds for the encampment of the army, for forts and palaces. 54 angulas are equal to 1 hasta used in measuring timber forests. 84 angulas are equal to 1 vyáma, used in measuring ropes and the depth of digging, in terms of a man's height. 4 aratnis are equal to 1 danda, 1 dhanus, 1 nálika and 1 paurusha. 108 angulas are equal to
AS-2.20.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 3 (AS-2.20.3)

AS-2.20.4.text: 1 garhapatya dhanus (i.e., a measure used by carpenters called grihapati). This measure is used in measuring roads and fort-walls. The same (108 angulas) are equal to 1 paurusha, a measure used in building sacrificial altars. 6 kamsas or 192 angulas are equal to 1 danda, used in measuring such lands as are gifted to Bráhmans. 10 dandas are equal to
AS-2.20.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 4 (AS-2.20.4)

AS-2.20.5.text: 1 rajju. 2 rajjus are equal to 1 paridesa (square measure). 3 rajjus are equal to 1 nivartana (square measure). The same (3 rajjus) plus 2 dandas on one side only are equal to 1 báhu (arm). 1000 dhanus are equal to 1 goruta (sound of a cow). 4 gorutas are equal to 1 yojana.
AS-2.20.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 5 (AS-2.20.5)

AS-2.20.6.text: (The divisions of time are) a truti, lava, nimesha, káshthá, kalá, náliká, muhúrta, forenoon, afternoon, day, night, paksha, month, ritu (season), ayana (solstice); samvatsara (year), and yuga. 2 trutis are equal to 1 lava. 2 lavas are equal to 1 nimesha. 5 nimeshas are equal to 1 káshthá. 30 káshthás are equal to 1 kalá. 40 kalás are equal to 1 náliká, or the time during which one ádhaka of water passes out of a pot through an aperture of the same diameter as that of a wire of 4 angulas in length and made of 4 máshas of gold. 2 nálikas are equal to 1 muhúrta. 15 muhúrtas are equal to 1 day or 1 night.
AS-2.20.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 6 (AS-2.20.6)

AS-2.20.7.text: Such a day and night happen in the months of Chaitra and Asvayuja. Then after the period of six months it increases or diminishes by three muhúrtas.
AS-2.20.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 7 (AS-2.20.7)

AS-2.20.8.text: When the length of shadow is eight paurushas (96 angulas), it is 1/18th part of the day.
AS-2.20.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 8 (AS-2.20.8)

AS-2.20.9.text: When it is 6 paurushas (72 angulas), it is 1/14th part of the day; when 4 paurushas, 1/8th part; when 2 paurushas, 1/6th part; when 1 paurusha, ¼th part; when it is 8 angulas, 3/10th part (trayodasabhágah); when 4 angulas, 3/8th part; and when no shadow is cast, it is to be considered midday.
AS-2.20.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 20, Sutra 9 (AS-2.20.9)

AS-2.21.1.text: THE Superintendent of Tolls shall erect near the large gate of the city both the toll-house and its flag facing either the north or the south. When merchants with their merchandise arrive at the toll-gate, four or five collectors shall take down who the merchants are, whence they come, what amount of merchandise they have brought and where for the first time the sealmark (abhijnánamudrá) has been made (on the merchandise).
AS-2.21.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 1 (AS-2.21.1)

AS-2.21.10.text: Those who smuggle a part of merchandise on which toll has not been paid with that on which toll has been paid as well as those who, with a view to smuggle with one pass a second portion of merchandise, put it along with the stamped merchandise after breaking open the bag shall forfeit the smuggled quantity and pay as much fine as is equal to the quantity so smuggled.
AS-2.21.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 10 (AS-2.21.10)

AS-2.21.11.text: He who, falsely swearing by cowdung, smuggles merchandise, shall be punished with the highest amercement.
AS-2.21.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 11 (AS-2.21.11)

AS-2.21.12.text: When a person imports such forbidden articles as weapons (sastra), mail armour, metals, chariots, precious stones, grains and cattle, he shall not only be punished as laid down elsewhere, but also be made to forfeit his merchandise. When any of such commodities has been brought in for sale, they shall be sold, free of toll far outside (the fort).
AS-2.21.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 12 (AS-2.21.12)

AS-2.21.13.text: The officer in charge of boundaries (antapála) shall receive a pana-and-a-quarter as roadcess (vartani) on each load of merchandise (panyavahanasya).
AS-2.21.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 13 (AS-2.21.13)

AS-2.21.14.text: He shall levy a pana on a single-hoofed animal, half a pana on each head of cattle, and a quarter on a minor quadruped.
AS-2.21.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 14 (AS-2.21.14)

AS-2.21.15.text: He shall also receive a másha on a head-load of merchandise.
AS-2.21.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 15 (AS-2.21.15)

AS-2.21.16.text: He shall also make good whatever has been lost by merchants (in the part of the country under his charge).
AS-2.21.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 16 (AS-2.21.16)

AS-2.21.17.text: After carefully examining foreign commodities as to their superior or inferior quality and stamping them with his seal, he shall send the same to the superintendent of tolls.
AS-2.21.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 17 (AS-2.21.17)

AS-2.21.18.text: Or he may send to the king a spy in the guise of a trader with information as to the quantity and quality of the merchandise. (Having received this information,) the king shall in turn send it to the superintendent of tolls in view of exhibiting the king's omniscient power. The superintendent shall tell the merchants (in question) that such and such a merchant has brought such and such amount of superior or inferior merchandise, which none can possibly hide, and that that information is due to the omniscient power of the king.
AS-2.21.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 18 (AS-2.21.18)

AS-2.21.19.text: For hiding inferior commodities, eight times the amount of toll shall be imposed; and for hiding or concealing superior commodities, they shall be wholly confiscated.
AS-2.21.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 19 (AS-2.21.19)

AS-2.21.2.text: Those whose merchandise has not been stamped with sealmark shall pay twice the amount of toll. For counterfeit seal they shall pay eight times the toll. If the sealmark is effaced or torn, (the merchants in question) shall be compelled to stand in ghatikásthána. When one kind of seal is used for another or when one kind of merchandise has been otherwise named (námakrite), the merchants shall pay a fine of 1¼ panás for each load (sapádapanikam vahanam dápayet).
AS-2.21.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 2 (AS-2.21.2)

AS-2.21.20.text: Whatever causes harm or is useless to the country shall be shut out; and whatever is of immense good as well as seeds not easily available shall be let in free of toll.
AS-2.21.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 20 (AS-2.21.20)

AS-2.21.3.text: The merchandise being placed near the flag of the toll-house, the merchants shall declare its quantity and price, cry out thrice "who will purchase this quantity of merchandise for this amount of price," and hand over the same to those who demand it (for that price). When purchasers happen to bid for it, the enhanced amount of the price together with the toll on the merchandise shall be paid into the king's treasury. When under the fear of having to pay a heavy toll, the quantity or the price of merchandise is lowered, the excess shall be taken by the king or the merchants shall be made to pay eight times the toll. The same punishment shall be imposed when the price of the merchandise packed in bags is lowered by showing an inferior sort as its sample or when valuable merchandise is covered over with a layer of an inferior one.
AS-2.21.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 3 (AS-2.21.3)

AS-2.21.4.text: When under the fear of bidders (enhancing the price), the price of any merchandise is increased beyond its proper value, the king shall receive the enhanced amount or twice the amount of toll on it. The same punishment or eight times the amount of toll shall be imposed on the Superintendent of tolls if he conceals (merchandise).
AS-2.21.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 4 (AS-2.21.4)

AS-2.21.5.text: Hence commodities shall be sold only after they are precisely weighed, measured, or numbered.
AS-2.21.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 5 (AS-2.21.5)

AS-2.21.6.text: With regard to inferior commodities as well as those which are to be let off free of toll, the amount of toll due shall be determined after careful consideration.
AS-2.21.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 6 (AS-2.21.6)

AS-2.21.7.text: Those merchants who pass beyond the flag of the toll-house without paying the toll shall be fined eight times the amount of the toll due from them.
AS-2.21.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 7 (AS-2.21.7)

AS-2.21.8.text: Those who pass by to and from (the city) shall ascertain (whether or not toll has been paid on any merchandise going along the road.)
AS-2.21.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 8 (AS-2.21.8)

AS-2.21.9.text: Commodities intended for marriages, or taken by a bride from her parents' house to her husband's (anváyanam), or intended for presentation, or taken for the purpose of sacrificial performance, confinement of women, worship of gods, ceremony of tonsure, investiture of sacred thread, gift of cows (godána, made before marriage), any religious rite, consecration ceremony (dikshá), and other special ceremonials shall be let off free of toll.
AS-2.21.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 21, Sutra 9 (AS-2.21.9)

AS-2.22.1.text: MERCHANDISE, external (báhyam, i.e., arriving from country parts), internal (ábhyantaram, i.e., manufactured inside forts), or foreign (átithyani, i.e., imported from foreign countries) shall all be liable to the payment of toll alike when exported (nishkrámya) and imported (pravésyam).
AS-2.22.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 22, Sutra 1 (AS-2.22.1)

AS-2.22.10.text: When vegetables, roots, bulbous roots are purchased from vegetable gardens, a fine 51¾ panas shall be imposed.
AS-2.22.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 22, Sutra 10 (AS-2.22.10)

AS-2.22.11.text: When any kind of grass or grain is purchased from field, a fine of 53 panas shall be imposed.
AS-2.22.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 22, Sutra 11 (AS-2.22.11)

AS-2.22.12.text: (Permanent) fines of 1 pana and 1½ panas shall be levied on agricultural produce (sítátyayah).
AS-2.22.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 22, Sutra 12 (AS-2.22.12)

AS-2.22.13.text: Hence in accordance with the customs of countries or of communities, the rate of toll shall be fixed on commodities, either old or new; and fines shall be fixed in proportion to the gravity of offences.
AS-2.22.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 22, Sutra 13 (AS-2.22.13)

AS-2.22.2.text: Imported commodities shall pay 1/5th of their value as toll.
AS-2.22.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 22, Sutra 2 (AS-2.22.2)

AS-2.22.3.text: Of flower, fruit, vegetables (sáka), roots (múla), bulbous roots (kanda), pallikya (?), seeds, dried fish, and dried meat, the superintendent shall receive 1/6th as toll.
AS-2.22.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 22, Sutra 3 (AS-2.22.3)

AS-2.22.4.text: As regards conch-shells, diamonds, precious stones, pearls, corals, and necklaces, experts acquainted with the time, cost, and finish of the production of such articles shall fix the amount of toll.
AS-2.22.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 22, Sutra 4 (AS-2.22.4)

AS-2.22.5.text: Of fibrous garments (kshauma), cotton cloths (dukúla), silk (krimitána), mail armour (kankata), sulphuret of arsenic (haritála), red arsenic (manassilá), vermilion (hingulaka), metals (lóha), and colouring ingredients (varnadhátu); of sandal, brown sandal (agaru), pungents (katuka), ferments (kinva), dress (ávarana), and the like; of wine, ivory, skins, raw materials used in making fibrous or cotton garments, carpets, curtains (právarana), and products yielded by worms (krimijáta); and of wool and other products yielded by goats and sheep, he shall receive 1/10th or 1/15th as toll.
AS-2.22.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 22, Sutra 5 (AS-2.22.5)

AS-2.22.6.text: Of cloths (vastra), quadrupeds, bipeds, threads, cotton, scents, medicines, wood, bamboo, fibres (valkala), skins, and clay-pots; of grains, oils, sugar (kshára), salt, liquor (madya) cooked rice and the like, he shall receive 1/20th or 1/25th as toll.
AS-2.22.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 22, Sutra 6 (AS-2.22.6)

AS-2.22.7.text: Gate-dues (dvárádeya) shall be 1/5th of toll dues; this tax may be remitted if circumstances necessitate such favour. Commodities shall never be sold where they are grown or manufactured.
AS-2.22.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 22, Sutra 7 (AS-2.22.7)

AS-2.22.8.text: When minerals and other commodities are purchased from mines, a fine of 600 panás shall be imposed.
AS-2.22.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 22, Sutra 8 (AS-2.22.8)

AS-2.22.9.text: When flower or fruits are purchased from flower or fruit gardens, a fine of 54 panas shall be imposed.
AS-2.22.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 22, Sutra 9 (AS-2.22.9)

AS-2.23.1.text: THE Superintendent of Weaving shall employ qualified persons to manufacture threads (sútra), coats (varma), cloths (vastra), and ropes.
AS-2.23.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 1 (AS-2.23.1)

AS-2.23.10.text: Those who are acquainted with the work shall manufacture mail armour.
AS-2.23.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 10 (AS-2.23.10)

AS-2.23.11.text: Those women who do not stir out of their houses (anishkásinyah), those whose husbands are gone abroad, and those who are cripple or girls may, when obliged to work for subsistence, be provided with work (spinning out threads) in due courtesy through the medium of maid-servants (of the weaving establishment.)
AS-2.23.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 11 (AS-2.23.11)

AS-2.23.12.text: Those women who can present themselves at the weaving house shall at dawn be enabled to exchange their spinnings for wages (bhándavetanavinimayam). Only so much light as is enough to examine the threads shall be kept. If the superintendent looks at the face of such women or talks about any other work, he shall be punished with the first amercement. Delay in paying the wages shall be punished with the middlemost amercement. Likewise when wages are paid for work that is not completed.
AS-2.23.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 12 (AS-2.23.12)

AS-2.23.13.text: She who, having received wages, does not turn out the work shall have her thumb cut off.
AS-2.23.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 13 (AS-2.23.13)

AS-2.23.14.text: Those who misappropriate, steal, or run away with, (the raw material supplied to them) shall be similarly punished.
AS-2.23.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 14 (AS-2.23.14)

AS-2.23.15.text: Weavers, when guilty, shall be fined out of their wages in proportion to their offences.
AS-2.23.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 15 (AS-2.23.15)

AS-2.23.16.text: The superintendent shall closely associate with those who manufacture ropes and mail armour and shall carry on the manufacture of straps (varatra) and other commodities.
AS-2.23.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 16 (AS-2.23.16)

AS-2.23.17.text: He shall carry on the manufacture of ropes from threads and fibres and of straps from cane and bamboo bark, with which beasts for draught are trained or tethered.
AS-2.23.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 17 (AS-2.23.17)

AS-2.23.2.text: Widows, cripple women, girls, mendicant or ascetic women (pravrajitá), women compelled to work in default of paying fines (dandápratikáriní), mothers of prostitutes, old women-servants of the king, and prostitutes (devadási) who have ceased to attend temples on service shall be employed to cut wool, fibre, cotton, panicle (túla), hemp, and flax.
AS-2.23.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 2 (AS-2.23.2)

AS-2.23.3.text: Wages shall be fixed according as the threads spun are fine, coarse (sthúla, i.e., big) or of middle quality and in proportion to a greater or less quantity manufactured, and in consideration of the quantity of thread spun, those (who turn out a greater quantity) shall be presented with oil and dried cakes of myrobalan fruits (tailámalakódvartanaih).
AS-2.23.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 3 (AS-2.23.3)

AS-2.23.4.text: They may also be made to work on holidays (tithishu) by payment of special rewards (prativápadánamánaih).
AS-2.23.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 4 (AS-2.23.4)

AS-2.23.5.text: Wages shall be cut short, if making allowance for the quality of raw material, the quantity of the threads spun out is found to fall short.
AS-2.23.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 5 (AS-2.23.5)

AS-2.23.6.text: Weaving may also be done by those artisans who are qualified to turn out a given amount of work in a given time and for a fixed amount of wages.
AS-2.23.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 6 (AS-2.23.6)

AS-2.23.7.text: The superintendent shall closely associate with the workmen.
AS-2.23.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 7 (AS-2.23.7)

AS-2.23.8.text: Those who manufacture fibrous cloths, raiments, silk-cloths, woollen cloths, and cotton fabrics shall be rewarded by presentations such as scents, garlands of flowers, or any other prizes of encouragement.
AS-2.23.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 8 (AS-2.23.8)

AS-2.23.9.text: Various kinds of garments, blankets, and curtains shall be manufactured.
AS-2.23.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 23, Sutra 9 (AS-2.23.9)

AS-2.24.1.text: POSSESSED of the knowledge of the science of agriculture dealing with the plantation of bushes and trees (krishitantragulmavrikshsháyurvedajñah), or assisted by those who are trained in such sciences, the superintendent of agriculture shall in time collect the seeds of all kinds of grains, flowers, fruits, vegetables, bulbous roots, roots, pállikya (?), fibre-producing plants, and cotton.
AS-2.24.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 1 (AS-2.24.1)

AS-2.24.10.text: Hence, i.e., according as the rainfall is more or less, the superintendent shall sow the seeds which require either more or less water.
AS-2.24.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 10 (AS-2.24.10)

AS-2.24.11.text: Sáli (a kind of rice), vríhi (rice), kodrava (Paspalum Scrobiculatum), tila (sesamum), priyangu (panic seeds), dáraka (?), and varaka (Phraseolus Trilobus) are to be sown at the commencement (púrvávápah) of the rainy season.
AS-2.24.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 11 (AS-2.24.11)

AS-2.24.12.text: Mudga (Phraseolus Mungo), másha (Phraseolus Radiatus), and saibya (?) are to be sown in the middle of the season.
AS-2.24.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 12 (AS-2.24.12)

AS-2.24.13.text: Kusumbha (safflower), masúra (Ervum Hirsutum), kuluttha (Dolichos Uniflorus), yava (barley), godhúma (wheat), kaláya (leguminus seeds), atasi (linseed), and sarshapa (mustard) are to be sown last.
AS-2.24.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 13 (AS-2.24.13)

AS-2.24.14.text: Or seeds may be sown according to the changes of the season.
AS-2.24.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 14 (AS-2.24.14)

AS-2.24.15.text: Fields that are left unsown (vápátiriktam, i.e., owing to the inadequacy of hands) may be brought under cultivation by employing those who cultivate for half the share in the produce (ardhasítiká); or those who live by their own physical exertion (svavíryopajívinah) may cultivate such fields for ¼th or 1/5th of the produce grown; or they may pay (to the king) as much as they can without entailing any hardship upon themselves (anavasitam bhágam), with the exception of their own private lands that are difficult to cultivate.
AS-2.24.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 15 (AS-2.24.15)

AS-2.24.16.text: Those who cultivate irrigating by manual labour (hastaprávartimam) shall pay 1/5th of the produce as water-rate (udakabhágam); by carrying water on shoulders (skandhaprávartimam) ¼th of the produce; by water-lifts (srotoyantraprávartimam), ⅓rd of the produce; and by raising water from rivers, lakes, tanks, and wells (nadisarastatákakúpodghátam),⅓rd or ¼th of the produce.
AS-2.24.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 16 (AS-2.24.16)

AS-2.24.17.text: The superintendent shall grow wet crops (kedára), winter-crops (haimana), or summer crops (graishmika) according to the supply of workmen and water.
AS-2.24.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 17 (AS-2.24.17)

AS-2.24.18.text: Rice-crops and the like are the best (jyáshtha, i.e., to grow); vegetables (shanda) are of intermediate nature; and sugarcane crops (ikshu) are the worst (pratyavarah, i.e., very difficult to grow), for they are subject to various evils and require much care and expenditure to reap.
AS-2.24.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 18 (AS-2.24.18)

AS-2.24.19.text: Lands that are beaten by foam (phenághátah, i.e., banks of rivers, etc.) are suitable for growing vallíphala (pumpkin, gourd and the like); lands that are frequently overflown by water (paríváhánta) for long pepper, grapes (mridvíká), and sugarcane; the vicinity of wells for vegetables and roots; low grounds (hariníparyantáh) for green crops; and marginal furrows between any two rows of crops are suitable for the plantation of fragrant plants, medicinal herbs, cascus roots (usínara), híra (?), beraka (?), and pindáluka (lac) and the like.
AS-2.24.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 19 (AS-2.24.19)

AS-2.24.2.text: He shall employ slaves, labourers, and prisoners (dandapratikartri) to sow the seeds on crown-lands which have been often and satisfactorily ploughed.
AS-2.24.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 2 (AS-2.24.2)

AS-2.24.20.text: Such medicinal herbs as grow in marshy grounds are to be grown not only in grounds suitable for them, but also in pots (sthályam).
AS-2.24.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 20 (AS-2.24.20)

AS-2.24.21.text: The seeds of grains are to be exposed to mist and heat (tushárapáyanamushnam cha) for seven nights; the seeds of kosi are treated similarly for three nights; the seeds of sugarcane and the like (kándabíjánam) are plastered at the cut end with the mixture of honey, clarified butter, the fat of hogs, and cowdung; the seeds of bulbous roots (kanda) with honey and clarified butter; cotton seeds (asthibíja) with cow-dung; and water pits at the root of trees are to be burnt and manured with the bones and dung of cows on proper occasions.
AS-2.24.21.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 21 (AS-2.24.21)

AS-2.24.22.text: The sprouts of seeds, when grown, are to be manured with a fresh haul of minute fishes and irrigated with the milk of snuhi (Euphorbia Antiquorum).
AS-2.24.22.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 22 (AS-2.24.22)

AS-2.24.23.text: Where there is the smoke caused by burning the essence of cotton seeds and the slough of a snake, there snakes will not stay.
AS-2.24.23.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 23 (AS-2.24.23)

AS-2.24.24.text: Always while sowing seeds, a handful of seeds bathed in water with a piece of gold shall be sown first and the following mantra recited:--
AS-2.24.24.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 24 (AS-2.24.24)

AS-2.24.25.text: “Prajápatye Kasyapáya déváya namah. Sadá Sítá medhyatám déví bíjéshu cha dhanéshu cha. Chandaváta hé."
AS-2.24.25.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 25 (AS-2.24.25)

AS-2.24.26.text: “Salutation to God Prajápati Kasyapa. Agriculture may always flourish and the Goddess (may reside) in seeds and wealth. Channdavata he."
AS-2.24.26.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 26 (AS-2.24.26)

AS-2.24.27.text: Provisions shall be supplied to watchmen, slaves and labourers in proportion to the amount of work done by them.
AS-2.24.27.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 27 (AS-2.24.27)

AS-2.24.28.text: They shall be paid a pana-and-a-quarter per mensem. Artisans shall be provided with wages and provision in proportion to the amount of work done by them.
AS-2.24.28.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 28 (AS-2.24.28)

AS-2.24.29.text: Those that are learned in the Vedas and those that are engaged in making penance may take from the fields ripe flowers and fruits for the purpose of worshipping their gods, and rice and barley for the purpose of performing ágrayana, a sacrificial performance at the commencement of harvest season, also those who live by gleaning grains in fields may gather grains where grains had been accumulated and removed from.
AS-2.24.29.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 29 (AS-2.24.29)

AS-2.24.3.text: The work of the above men shall not suffer on account of any want in ploughs (karshanayantra) and other necessary instruments or of bullocks. Nor shall there be any delay in procuring to them the assistence of blacksmiths, carpenters, borers (medaka), ropemakers, as well as those who catch snakes, and similar persons.
AS-2.24.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 3 (AS-2.24.3)

AS-2.24.30.text: Grains and other crops shall be collected as often as they are harvested. No wise man shall leave anything in the fields, nor even chaff. Crops, when reaped, shall be heaped up in high piles or in the form of turrets. The piles of crops shall not be kept close, nor shall their tops be small or low. The threshing floors of different fields shall be situated close to each other. Workmen in the fields shall always have water but no fire.
AS-2.24.30.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 30 (AS-2.24.30)

AS-2.24.4.text: Any loss due to the above persons shall be punished with a fine equal to the loss.
AS-2.24.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 4 (AS-2.24.4)

AS-2.24.5.text: The quantity of rain that falls in the country of jángala is 16 dronas; half as much more in moist countries (anúpánám); as to the countries which are fit for agriculture (désavápánam);--13½ dronas in the country of asmakas; 23 dronas in avantí; and an immense quantity in western countries (aparántánám), the borders of the Himalayas, and the countries where water channels are made use of in agriculture (kulyávápánám).
AS-2.24.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 5 (AS-2.24.5)

AS-2.24.6.text: When one-third of the requisite quantity of rain falls both during the commencement and closing months of the rainy season and two-thirds in the middle, then the rainfall is (considered) very even (sushumárúpam).
AS-2.24.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 6 (AS-2.24.6)

AS-2.24.7.text: A forecast of such rainfall can be made by observing the position, motion, and pregnancy (garbhádána) of the Jupiter (Brihaspati), the rise and set and motion of the Venus, and the natural or unnatural aspect of the sun.
AS-2.24.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 7 (AS-2.24.7)

AS-2.24.8.text: From the sun, the sprouting of the seeds can be inferred; from (the position of) the Jupiter, the formation of grains (stambakarita) can be inferred; and from the movements of the Venus, rainfall can be inferred.
AS-2.24.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 8 (AS-2.24.8)

AS-2.24.9.text: Three are the clouds that continuously rain for seven days; eighty are they that pour minute drops; and sixty are they that appear with the sunshine--this is termed rainfall. Where rain, free from wind and unmingled with sunshine, falls so as to render three turns of ploughing possible, there the reaping of good harvest is certain.
AS-2.24.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 24, Sutra 9 (AS-2.24.9)

AS-2.25.1.text: BY employing such men as are acquainted with the manufacture of liquor and ferments (kinva), the Superintendent of Liquor shall carry on liquor-traffic not only in forts and country parts, but also in camps.
AS-2.25.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 1 (AS-2.25.1)

AS-2.25.10.text: When customers under intoxication lose any of their things, the merchants of the shop shall not only make good the loss, but also pay an equivalent fine.
AS-2.25.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 10 (AS-2.25.10)

AS-2.25.11.text: Merchants seated in half-closed rooms shall observe the appearance of local and foreign customers who, in real or false guise of Aryas lie down in intoxication along with their beautiful mistresses.
AS-2.25.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 11 (AS-2.25.11)

AS-2.25.12.text: Of various kinds of liquor such as medaka, prasanna, ásava, arista, maireya, and madhu:--
AS-2.25.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 12 (AS-2.25.12)

AS-2.25.13.text: Medaka is manufactured with one drona of water, half, an ádaka of rice, and three prastha of kinva (ferment).
AS-2.25.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 13 (AS-2.25.13)

AS-2.25.14.text: Twelve ádhakas of flour (pishta), five prasthas of kinva (ferment), with the addition of spices (játisambhára) together with the bark and fruits of putraká (a species of tree) constitute prasanná.
AS-2.25.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 14 (AS-2.25.14)

AS-2.25.15.text: One-hundred palas of kapittha (Feronia Elephantum) 500 palas of phánita (sugar), and one prastha of honey (madhu) form ásava.
AS-2.25.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 15 (AS-2.25.15)

AS-2.25.16.text: With an increase of one-quarter of the above ingredients, a superior kind of ásava is manufactured; and when the same ingredients are lessened to the extent of one-quarter each, it becomes of an inferior quality.
AS-2.25.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 16 (AS-2.25.16)

AS-2.25.17.text: The preparation of various kinds of arishta for various diseases are to be learnt from physicians.
AS-2.25.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 17 (AS-2.25.17)

AS-2.25.18.text: A sour gruel or decoction of the bark of meshasringi (a kind of poison) mixed with jaggery (guda) and with the powder of long pepper and black pepper or with the powder of triphala (1 Terminalia Chebula, 2 Terminalia Bellerica, and 3 Phyllanthus Emblica) forms Maireya.
AS-2.25.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 18 (AS-2.25.18)

AS-2.25.19.text: To all kinds of liquor mixed with jaggery, the powder of triphala is always added.
AS-2.25.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 19 (AS-2.25.19)

AS-2.25.2.text: In accordance with the requirements of demand and supply (krayavikrayavasena) he may either centralize or decentralize the sale of liquor.
AS-2.25.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 2 (AS-2.25.2)

AS-2.25.20.text: The juice of grapes is termed madhu. Its own native place (svadesa) is the commentary on such of its various forms as kápisáyana and hárahúraka.
AS-2.25.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 20 (AS-2.25.20)

AS-2.25.21.text: One drona of either boiled or unboiled paste of másha (Phraseolus Radiatus), three parts more of rice, and one karsha of morata (Alangium Hexapetalum) and the like form kinva (ferment).
AS-2.25.21.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 21 (AS-2.25.21)

AS-2.25.22.text: In the manufacture of medaka and prasanna, five karshas of the powder of (each of páthá (Clypea Hermandifolio), lodhra (Symplocos Racemosa), tejovati (Piper Chaba), eláváluka (Solanum Melongena) honey, the juice of grapes (madhurasa), priyangu (panic seeds), dáruharidra (a species of turmeric) black pepper and long pepper are added as sambhára, requisite spices.
AS-2.25.22.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 22 (AS-2.25.22)

AS-2.25.23.text: The decoction of madhúka (Bassia Latifolia) mixed with granulated sugar (katasarkará), when added to prasanna, gives it a pleasing colour.
AS-2.25.23.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 23 (AS-2.25.23)

AS-2.25.24.text: The requisite quantity of spices to be added to ásava is one karshá of the powder of each of chocha (bark of cinnamon), chitraka (Plumbago Zeylanica), vilanga, and gajapippalí (Scindapsus Officinalis), and two karshas of the powder of each of kramuka (betel nut), madhúka (Bassia Latifolia), mustá (Cyprus Rotundus), and lodhra (Symlocos Racemosa).
AS-2.25.24.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 24 (AS-2.25.24)

AS-2.25.25.text: The addition of one-tenth of the above ingredients (i.e., chocha, kramuka, etc.), is (termed) bíjabandha.
AS-2.25.25.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 25 (AS-2.25.25)

AS-2.25.26.text: The same ingredients as are added to prasanná are also added to white liquor (svetasurá).
AS-2.25.26.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 26 (AS-2.25.26)

AS-2.25.27.text: The liquor that is manufactured from mango fruits (sahakárasurá) may contain a greater proportion of mango essence (rasottara), or of spices (bíjottara). It is called mahásura when it contains sambhára (spices as described above).
AS-2.25.27.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 27 (AS-2.25.27)

AS-2.25.28.text: When a handful (antarnakho mushtih, i.e., so much as can be held in the hand, the fingers being so bent that the nails cannot be seen) of the powder of granulated sugar dissolved in the decoction of moratá (Alangium Hexapetalum), palása (Butea Frondosa), dattúra (Dattura Fastuosa), karanja (Robinia Mitis), meshasringa (a kind of poison) and the bark of milky trees (kshiravriksha) mixed with one-half of the paste formed by combining the powders of lodhra (Symplocos Racemosa), chitraka (Plumbago Zeylanica), vilanga, páthá (clypea Hermandifolia), mustá (cyprus Rotundus), kaláya (leguminous seeds), dáruharidra (Amonum Xanthorrhizon), indívara (blue lotus), satapushpa (Anethum Sowa), apámárga (Achyranthes Aspera) saptaparna (Echites Scholaris), and nimba (Nimba Melia) is added to (even) a kumbha of liquor payable by the king, it renders it very pleasant.
AS-2.25.28.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 28 (AS-2.25.28)

AS-2.25.29.text: Five palas of phánita (sugar) are added to the above in order to increase its flavour.
AS-2.25.29.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 29 (AS-2.25.29)

AS-2.25.3.text: A fine of 600 panas shall be imposed on all offenders other than those who are manufacturers, purchasers, or sellers in liquor-traffic.
AS-2.25.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 3 (AS-2.25.3)

AS-2.25.30.text: On special occasions (krityeshu), people (kutumbinah, i.e., families) shall be allowed to manufacture white liquor (svetasura), arishta for use in diseases, and other kinds of liquor.
AS-2.25.30.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 30 (AS-2.25.30)

AS-2.25.31.text: On the occasions of festivals, fairs (samája), and pilgrimage, right of manufacture of liquor for four days (chaturahassaurikah) shall be allowed.
AS-2.25.31.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 31 (AS-2.25.31)

AS-2.25.32.text: The Superintendent shall collect the daily fines (daivasikamatyayam, i.e., license fees) from those who on these occasions are permitted to manufacture liquor.
AS-2.25.32.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 32 (AS-2.25.32)

AS-2.25.33.text: Women and children shall collect ‘sura,’ and ‘kinva,’ ‘ferment.’
AS-2.25.33.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 33 (AS-2.25.33)

AS-2.25.34.text: Those who deal with liquor other than that of the king shall pay five percent as toll.
AS-2.25.34.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 34 (AS-2.25.34)

AS-2.25.35.text: With regard to sura, medaka, arishta, wine, phalámla (acid drinks prepared from fruits), and ámlasídhu (spirit distilled from molasses):--
AS-2.25.35.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 35 (AS-2.25.35)

AS-2.25.36.text: Having ascertained the day's sale of the above kinds of liquor, the difference of royal and public measures (mánavyáji), and the excessive amount of sale proceeds realised thereby, the Superintendent shall fix the amount of compensation (vaidharana) due to the king (from local or foreign merchants for entailing loss on the king's liquor traffic) and shall always adopt the best course.
AS-2.25.36.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 36 (AS-2.25.36)

AS-2.25.4.text: Liquor shall not be taken out of villages, nor shall liquor shops be close to each other.
AS-2.25.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 4 (AS-2.25.4)

AS-2.25.5.text: Lest workmen spoil the work in hand, and Aryas violate their decency and virtuous character, and lest firebrands commit indiscreet acts, liquor shall be sold to persons of well known character in such small quantities as one-fourth or half-a-kudumba, one kudumba, half-a-prastha, or one prastha. Those who are well known and of pure character may take liquor out of shop.
AS-2.25.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 5 (AS-2.25.5)

AS-2.25.6.text: Or all may be compelled to drink liquor within the shops and not allowed to stir out at once in view of detecting articles such as sealed deposits, unsealed deposits, commodities given for repair, stolen articles, and the like which the customer's may have acquired by foul means. When they are found to possess gold and other articles not their own, the superintendent shall contrive to cause them to be arrested outside the shop. Likewise those who are too extravagant or spend beyond their income shall be arrested.
AS-2.25.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 6 (AS-2.25.6)

AS-2.25.7.text: No fresh liquor other than bad liquor shall be sold below its price. Bad liquor may be sold elsewhere or given to slaves or workmen in lieu of wages; or it may form the drink of beasts for draught or the subsistence of hogs.
AS-2.25.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 7 (AS-2.25.7)

AS-2.25.8.text: Liquor shops shall contain many rooms provided with beds and seats kept apart. The drinking room shall contain scents, garlands of flowers, water, and other comfortable things suitable to the varying seasons.
AS-2.25.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 8 (AS-2.25.8)

AS-2.25.9.text: Spies stationed in the shops shall ascertain whether the expenditure incurred by customers in the shop is ordinary or extraordinary and also whether there are any strangers. They shall also ascertain the value of the dress, ornaments, and gold of the customers lying there under intoxication.
AS-2.25.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 25, Sutra 9 (AS-2.25.9)

AS-2.26.1.text: WHEN a person entraps, kills, or molests deer, bison, birds, and fish which are declared to be under State protection or which live in forests under State-protection (abhayáranya), he shall be punished with the highest amercement.
AS-2.26.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 1 (AS-2.26.1)

AS-2.26.10.text: If there is any diminution in weight owing to the use of a false balance, they shall give eight times the diminution.
AS-2.26.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 10 (AS-2.26.10)

AS-2.26.11.text: Cattle such as a calf, a bull, or a milch cow shall not be slaughtered.
AS-2.26.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 11 (AS-2.26.11)

AS-2.26.12.text: He who slaughters or tortures them to death shall be fined 50 panas.
AS-2.26.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 12 (AS-2.26.12)

AS-2.26.13.text: The flesh of animals which have been killed outside the slaughter-house (parisúnam), headless, legless and boneless flesh, rotten flesh, and the flesh of animals which have suddenly died shall not be sold. Otherwise a fine of 12 panas shall be imposed.
AS-2.26.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 13 (AS-2.26.13)

AS-2.26.14.text: Cattle, wild beasts, elephants (vyala), and fish living in forests under State protection shall, if they become of vicious nature, be entrapped and killed outside the forest preserve.
AS-2.26.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 14 (AS-2.26.14)

AS-2.26.2.text: Householders trespassing in forest preserves shall be punished with the middlemost amercement.
AS-2.26.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 2 (AS-2.26.2)

AS-2.26.3.text: When a person entraps, kills, or molests either fish or birds that do not prey upon other animals, he shall be fined 26¾ panas; and when he does the same to deer and other beasts, he shall be fined twice as much.
AS-2.26.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 3 (AS-2.26.3)

AS-2.26.4.text: Of beasts of prey that have been captured, the Superintendent shall take one-sixth; of fish and birds (of similar nature), he shall take one-tenth or more than one-tenth; and of deer and other beasts (mrigapasu), one-tenth or more than one-tenth as toll.
AS-2.26.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 4 (AS-2.26.4)

AS-2.26.5.text: One-sixth of live animals such as birds and beasts shall be let off in forests under State-protection.
AS-2.26.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 5 (AS-2.26.5)

AS-2.26.6.text: Elephants, horses or animals having the form of a man, bull or an ass living in oceans as well as fish in tanks, lakes, channels and rivers; and such game-birds as krauncha (a kind of heron), utkrosaka (osprey), dátyúha (a sort of cuckoo), hamsa (flamingo), chakraváka (a brahmany duck), jivanjívaka (a kind of pheasant), bhringarája (Lanius Malabaricus), chakora (partridge), mattakokila (cuckoo), peacock, parrot, and maina (madanasárika) as well as other auspicious animals, whether birds or beasts, shall be protected from all kinds of molestations.
AS-2.26.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 6 (AS-2.26.6)

AS-2.26.7.text: Those who violate the above rule shall be punished with the first amercement.
AS-2.26.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 7 (AS-2.26.7)

AS-2.26.8.text: (Butchers) shall sell fresh and boneless flesh of beasts (mrigapasu) just killed.
AS-2.26.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 8 (AS-2.26.8)

AS-2.26.9.text: If they sell bony flesh, they shall give an equivalent compensation (pratipákam).
AS-2.26.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 26, Sutra 9 (AS-2.26.9)

AS-2.27.1.text: THE Superintendent of Prostitutes shall employ (at the king's court) on a salary of 1,000 panas (per annum) a prostitute (ganiká), whether born or not born of a prostitute's family, and noted for her beauty, youth, and accomplishments.
AS-2.27.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 1 (AS-2.27.1)

AS-2.27.10.text: The superintendent shall determine the earnings, inheritance, income (áya), expenditure, and future earnings (áyati) of every prostitute.
AS-2.27.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 10 (AS-2.27.10)

AS-2.27.11.text: When a prostitute puts her jewellery in the hands of any person but her mother, she shall be fined 4¼ panas.
AS-2.27.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 11 (AS-2.27.11)

AS-2.27.12.text: If she sells or mortgages her property (svapateyam), she shall be fined 50¼ panas.
AS-2.27.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 12 (AS-2.27.12)

AS-2.27.13.text: A prostitute shall be fined 24 panas for defamation; twice as much for causing hurt; and 50¼ panas as well as 1½ panas for cutting off the ear (of any person).
AS-2.27.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 13 (AS-2.27.13)

AS-2.27.14.text: When a man has connection with a prostitute against her will or with a prostitute girl (kumári), he shall be punished with the highest amercement. But when he has connection with a willing prostitute, (under age), he shall be punished with the first amercement.
AS-2.27.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 14 (AS-2.27.14)

AS-2.27.15.text: When a man keeps under confinement, or abducts, a prostitute against her will, or disfigures her by causing hurt, he shall be fined 1,000 panas or more rising up to twice the amount of her ransom (nishkraya) according to the circumstances of the crime and the position and the status of the prostitute (sthánaviseshena).
AS-2.27.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 15 (AS-2.27.15)

AS-2.27.16.text: When a man causes hurt to a prostitute appointed at the court (praptádhikáram), he shall be fined thrice the amount of her ransom.
AS-2.27.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 16 (AS-2.27.16)

AS-2.27.17.text: When a man causes hurt to a prostitute's mother, to her young daughter, or to a rúpadási, he shall be punished with the highest amercement.
AS-2.27.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 17 (AS-2.27.17)

AS-2.27.18.text: In all cases of offences, punishment for offences committed for the first time shall be the first amercement; twice as much for offences committed for a second time; thrice as much for the third time; and for offences committed for the fourth time, the king may impose any punishment he likes.
AS-2.27.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 18 (AS-2.27.18)

AS-2.27.19.text: When a prostitute does not yield her person to any one under the orders of the king, she shall receive 1000 lashes with a whip or pay a fine of 5,000 panas.
AS-2.27.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 19 (AS-2.27.19)

AS-2.27.2.text: A rival prostitute (pratiganiká) on half the above salary (kutumbárdhéna) shall also be appointed.
AS-2.27.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 2 (AS-2.27.2)

AS-2.27.20.text: When having received the requisite amount of fees, a prostitute dislikes to yield her person, she shall be fined twice the amount of the fees.
AS-2.27.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 20 (AS-2.27.20)

AS-2.27.21.text: When, in her own house, a prostitute deprives her paramour of his enjoyment, she shall be fined eight times the amount of the fees unless the paramour happens to be unassociable on account of disease and personal defects.
AS-2.27.21.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 21 (AS-2.27.21)

AS-2.27.22.text: When a prostitute murders her paramour, she shall be burnt alive or thrown into water.
AS-2.27.22.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 22 (AS-2.27.22)

AS-2.27.23.text: When a paramour steals the jewellery or money of, or deceives to pay the fees due to, a prostitute, he shall be fined eight times that amount.
AS-2.27.23.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 23 (AS-2.27.23)

AS-2.27.24.text: Every prostitute shall supply information to the superintendent as to the amount of her daily fees (bhoga), her future income (áyati), and the paramour (under her influence).
AS-2.27.24.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 24 (AS-2.27.24)

AS-2.27.25.text: The same rules shall apply to an actor, dancer, singer, player on musical instruments, a buffoon (vágjivana), a mimic player (kusílava), rope-dancer (plavaka), a juggler (saubhika), a wandering bard or herald (chárana), pimps, and unchaste women.
AS-2.27.25.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 25 (AS-2.27.25)

AS-2.27.26.text: When persons of the above description come from foreign countries to hold their performances, they shall pay 5 panas as license fee (prekshávetana).
AS-2.27.26.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 26 (AS-2.27.26)

AS-2.27.27.text: Every prostitute (rúpájivá) shall pay every month twice the amount of a day's earning (bhogadvigunam) to the Government.
AS-2.27.27.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 27 (AS-2.27.27)

AS-2.27.28.text: Those who teach prostitutes, female slaves, and actresses, arts such as singing, playing on musical instruments, reading, dancing, acting, writing, painting, playing on the instruments like vina, pipe, and drum, reading the thoughts of others, manufacture of scents and garlands, shampooing, and the art of attracting and captivating the mind of others shall be endowed with maintenance from the State.
AS-2.27.28.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 28 (AS-2.27.28)

AS-2.27.29.text: They (the teachers) shall train the sons of prostitutes to be chief actors (rangopajívi) on the stage.
AS-2.27.29.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 29 (AS-2.27.29)

AS-2.27.3.text: Whenever such a prostitute goes abroad or dies, her daughter or sister shall act for her and receive her property and salary. Or her mother may substitute another prostitute. In the absence of any of these, the king himself shall take the property.
AS-2.27.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 3 (AS-2.27.3)

AS-2.27.30.text: The wives of actors and others of similar profession who have been taught various languages and the use of signals (sanja) shall, along with their relatives, be made use of in detecting the wicked and murdering or deluding foreign spies.
AS-2.27.30.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 30 (AS-2.27.30)

AS-2.27.4.text: With a view to add to the splendour of prostitutes holding the royal umbrella, golden pitcher, and fan, and attending upon the king seated on his royal litter, throne, or chariot, prostitutes shall be classified as of first, middle and highest rank according to their beauty and splendid jewellery; likewise their salary shall be fixed by thousands.
AS-2.27.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 4 (AS-2.27.4)

AS-2.27.5.text: She who has lost her beauty shall be appointed as a nurse (mátriká).
AS-2.27.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 5 (AS-2.27.5)

AS-2.27.6.text: A prostitute shall pay 24,000 panas as ransom to regain her liberty; and a prostitute's son 12,000 panas.
AS-2.27.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 6 (AS-2.27.6)

AS-2.27.7.text: From the age of eight years, a prostitute shall hold musical performance before the king.
AS-2.27.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 7 (AS-2.27.7)

AS-2.27.8.text: Those prostitutes, female slaves, and old women who are incapable of rendering any service in the form of enjoyment (bhagnabhogáh) shall work in the storehouse or kitchen of the king.
AS-2.27.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 8 (AS-2.27.8)

AS-2.27.9.text: A prostitute who, putting herself under the protection of a private person, ceases to attend the king's court shall pay a pana-and-a-quarter per mensem (to the Government).
AS-2.27.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 27, Sutra 9 (AS-2.27.9)

AS-2.28.1.text: THE Superintendent of Ships shall examine the accounts relating to navigation not only on oceans and mouths of rivers, but also on lakes natural or artificial, and rivers in the vicinity of stháníya and other fortified cities.
AS-2.28.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 1 (AS-2.28.1)

AS-2.28.10.text: Vessels carrying on merchandise spoiled by water may either be exempted from toll or may have their toll reduced to half and let to sail when the time for setting sail approaches.
AS-2.28.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 10 (AS-2.28.10)

AS-2.28.11.text: Ships that touch at harbours on their way may be requested the payment of toll.
AS-2.28.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 11 (AS-2.28.11)

AS-2.28.12.text: Pirate ships (himsríká), vessels which are bound for the country of an enemy, as well as those which have violated the customs and rules in force in port towns shall be destroyed.
AS-2.28.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 12 (AS-2.28.12)

AS-2.28.13.text: In those large rivers which cannot be forded even during the winter and summer seasons, there shall be launched large boats (mahánávah) provided with a captain (sásaka), a steersman (niyámaka), and servants to hold the sickle and the ropes and to pour out water.
AS-2.28.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 13 (AS-2.28.13)

AS-2.28.14.text: Small boats shall be launched in those small rivers which overflow during the rainy season.
AS-2.28.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 14 (AS-2.28.14)

AS-2.28.15.text: Fording or crossing the rivers (without permission) shall be prohibited lest traitors may cross them (and escape).
AS-2.28.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 15 (AS-2.28.15)

AS-2.28.16.text: When a person fords or crosses a river outside the proper place and in unusual times, he shall be punished with the first amercement.
AS-2.28.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 16 (AS-2.28.16)

AS-2.28.17.text: When a man fords or crosses a river at the usual place and time without permission, he shall be fined 26¾ panas.
AS-2.28.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 17 (AS-2.28.17)

AS-2.28.18.text: Fishermen, carriers of firewood, grass, flowers, and fruits, gardeners, vegetable-dealers, and herdsmen, persons pursuing suspected criminals, messengers following other messengers going in advance, servants engaged to carry things, provisions, and orders to the army, those who use their own ferries, as well as those who supply villages of marshy districts with seeds, necessaries of life, commodities and other accessary things shall be exempted (to cross rivers at any time and place).
AS-2.28.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 18 (AS-2.28.18)

AS-2.28.19.text: Bráhmans, ascetics (pravrajita), children, the aged, the afflicted, royal messengers, and pregnant women shall be provided by the superintendent with free passes to cross rivers.
AS-2.28.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 19 (AS-2.28.19)

AS-2.28.2.text: Villages on seashores or on the banks of rivers and lakes shall pay a fixed amount of tax (kliptam).
AS-2.28.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 2 (AS-2.28.2)

AS-2.28.20.text: Foreign merchants who have often been visiting the country as well as those who are well known to local merchants shall be allowed to land in port-towns.
AS-2.28.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 20 (AS-2.28.20)

AS-2.28.21.text: Any person who is abducting the wife or daughter of another, one who is carrying off the wealth of another, a suspected person, one who seems to be of perturbed appearance, one who has no baggage, one who attempts to conceal, or evade the cognisance of the valuable load in one's hand, one who has just put on a different garb, one who has removed or renounced one's usual garb, one who has just turned out an ascetic, one who pretends to be suffering from disease, one who seems to be alarmed, one who is stealthily carrying valuable things, or going on a secret mission, or carrying weapons or explosives (agniyoga), one who holds poison in one's hand, and one who has come from a long distance without a pass shall all be arrested.
AS-2.28.21.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 21 (AS-2.28.21)

AS-2.28.22.text: A minor quadruped as well as a man carrying some load shall pay one másha.
AS-2.28.22.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 22 (AS-2.28.22)

AS-2.28.23.text: A head-load, a load carried on shoulders (káyabhárah), a cow, and a horse shall each pay 2 máshas.
AS-2.28.23.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 23 (AS-2.28.23)

AS-2.28.24.text: A small cart (laghuyána) 5 máshas; and a cart (of medium size) drawn by bulls (golingam) shall pay 6 máshas and a big cart (sakata) 7 máshas.
AS-2.28.24.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 24 (AS-2.28.24)

AS-2.28.25.text: A head-load of merchandise ¼ másha; this explains other kinds of loads. In big rivers, ferry-fees are double the above. Villages near marshy places shall give (to the ferry-men) the prescribed amount of food-stuff and wages.
AS-2.28.25.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 25 (AS-2.28.25)

AS-2.28.26.text: In boundaries, ferry-men shall receive the toll, carriage-cess, and road-cess. They shall also confiscate the property of the person travelling without a pass. The Superintendent of Boats shall make good the loss caused by the loss of the boat due to the heavy load, sailing in improper time or place, want of ferry-men, or lack of repair. Boats should be launched between the months of Ashádha, the first seven days being omitted, and Kártika; the evidence of a ferryman should be given and the daily income should be remitted.
AS-2.28.26.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 26 (AS-2.28.26)

AS-2.28.3.text: Fishermen shall give 1/6th of their haul as fees for fishing license (naukáhátakam).
AS-2.28.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 3 (AS-2.28.3)

AS-2.28.4.text: Merchants shall pay the customary toll levied in port-towns.
AS-2.28.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 4 (AS-2.28.4)

AS-2.28.5.text: Passengers arriving on board the king's ship shall pay the requisite amount of sailing fees (yátrávetanam).
AS-2.28.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 5 (AS-2.28.5)

AS-2.28.6.text: Those (who make use of the king’s boats in) fishing out conch-shells and pearls shall pay the requisite amount of hire (Naukáhátakam), or they may make use of their own boats.
AS-2.28.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 6 (AS-2.28.6)

AS-2.28.7.text: The duties of the superintendent of mines will explain those of the superintendent of conch-shells and pearls.
AS-2.28.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 7 (AS-2.28.7)

AS-2.28.8.text: The superintendent of ships shall strictly observe the customs prevalent in commercial towns as well as the orders of the superintendent of towns (pattana, port town).
AS-2.28.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 8 (AS-2.28.8)

AS-2.28.9.text: Whenever a weatherbeaten ship arrives at a port-town, he shall show fatherly kindness to it.
AS-2.28.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 28, Sutra 9 (AS-2.28.9)

AS-2.29.1.text: THE Superintendent of cows shall supervise (1) herds maintained for wages (vétanópagráhikam), (2) herds surrendered for a fixed amount of dairy produce (karapratikara), (3) useless and abandoned herds (bhagnotsrishtakam), (4) herds maintained for a share in dairy produce (bhágánupravishtam), (5) classes of herds (vrajaparyagram), (6) cattle that strayed (nashtam), (7) cattle that are irrecoverably lost (vinashtam), and (8) the amassed quantity of milk and clarified butter.
AS-2.29.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 1 (AS-2.29.1)

AS-2.29.10.text: Whoever hurts or causes another to hurt, or steals or causes another to steal a cow, should be slain.
AS-2.29.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 10 (AS-2.29.10)

AS-2.29.11.text: When a person substitutes an animal (rúpa) bearing the royal brand mark for a private one, he shall be punished with the first amercement.
AS-2.29.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 11 (AS-2.29.11)

AS-2.29.12.text: When a person recovers a local cattle from thieves, he shall receive the promised reward (panitam rúpam); and when a man rescues a foreign cattle (from thieves), he shall receive half its value.
AS-2.29.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 12 (AS-2.29.12)

AS-2.29.13.text: Cowherds shall apply remedies to calves or aged cows or cows suffering from diseases.
AS-2.29.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 13 (AS-2.29.13)

AS-2.29.14.text: They shall graze the herds in forests which are severally allotted as pasture grounds for various seasons and from which thieves, tigers and other molesting beasts are driven away by hunters aided by their hounds.
AS-2.29.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 14 (AS-2.29.14)

AS-2.29.15.text: With a view to scare out snakes and tigers and as a definite means of knowing the whereabouts of herds, sounding bells shall be attached to (the neck of) timid cattle.
AS-2.29.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 15 (AS-2.29.15)

AS-2.29.16.text: Cowherds shall allow their cattle to enter into such rivers or lakes as are of equal depth all round, broad, and free from mire and crocodiles, and shall protect them from dangers under such circumstances.
AS-2.29.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 16 (AS-2.29.16)

AS-2.29.17.text: Whenever an animal is caught hold of by a thief, a tiger, a snake, or a crocodile, or when it is too infirm owing to age or disease, they shall make a report of it; otherwise they shall be compelled to make good the loss.
AS-2.29.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 17 (AS-2.29.17)

AS-2.29.18.text: When an animal dies a natural death, they shall surrender the skin with the brand mark, if it is a cow or a buffalo; the skin together with the ear (karnalakshanam) if it is a goat or sheep; the tail with the skin containing the brand mark, if it is an ass or a camel; the skin, if it is a young one; besides the above, (they shall also restore) the fat (vasti), bile, marrow (snáyu), teeth, hoofs, horns, and bones.
AS-2.29.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 18 (AS-2.29.18)

AS-2.29.19.text: They (the cowherds) may sell either fresh flesh or dried flesh.
AS-2.29.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 19 (AS-2.29.19)

AS-2.29.2.text: (1) When a cowherd, a buffalo-herdsman, a milker, a churner, and a hunter (lubdhaka) fed by wages graze milch cows (dhenu) in hundreds (satam satam)--for if they graze the herds for the profit of milk and ghi, they will starve the calves to death,--that system of rearing the cattle is termed ‘herds maintained for wages.’
AS-2.29.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 2 (AS-2.29.2)

AS-2.29.20.text: They shall give buttermilk as drink to dogs and hogs, and reserve a little (buttermilk) in a bronze vessel to prepare their own dish: they may also make use of coagulated milk or cheese (kíláta) to render their oilcakes relishing (ghánapinyáka-kledartha).
AS-2.29.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 20 (AS-2.29.20)

AS-2.29.21.text: He who sells his cow (from among the herds) shall pay (to the king) ¼th rúpa (value of the cow).
AS-2.29.21.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 21 (AS-2.29.21)

AS-2.29.22.text: During the rainy, autumnal, and the first part of winter (hemanta) seasons, they shall milk the cattle both the times (morning and evening); and during the latter part of winter and the whole of the spring and summer seasons, they shall milk only once (i.e., only in the morning). The cowherd who milks a cow a second time during these seasons shall have his thumb cut off.
AS-2.29.22.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 22 (AS-2.29.22)

AS-2.29.23.text: If he allows the time of milking to lapse, he shall forfeit the profit thereof (i.e., the milk).
AS-2.29.23.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 23 (AS-2.29.23)

AS-2.29.24.text: The same rule shall hold good in case of negligence of the opportune moment for putting a string through the nose of a bull and other animals, and for taming or training them to the yoke.
AS-2.29.24.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 24 (AS-2.29.24)

AS-2.29.25.text: One drona of a cow's milk will, when churned, yield one prastha of butter; the same quantity of a buffalo's milk will yield 1/7th prastha more; and the same quantity of milk of goats and sheep will produce ½ prastha more.
AS-2.29.25.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 25 (AS-2.29.25)

AS-2.29.26.text: In all kinds of milk, the exact quantity of butter shall be ascertained by churning; for increase in the supply of milk and butter depends on the nature of the soil and the quantity and quality of fodder and water.
AS-2.29.26.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 26 (AS-2.29.26)

AS-2.29.27.text: When a person causes a bull attached to a herd to fight with another bull, he shall be punished with the first amercement; when a bull is injured (under such circumstances), he shall be punished with the highest amercement.
AS-2.29.27.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 27 (AS-2.29.27)

AS-2.29.28.text: Cattle shall be grouped in herds of ten each of similar colour, while they are being grazed.
AS-2.29.28.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 28 (AS-2.29.28)

AS-2.29.29.text: According to the protective strength of the cowherds the capacity of the cattle to go far and wide to graze, cowherds shall take their cattle either far or near.
AS-2.29.29.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 29 (AS-2.29.29)

AS-2.29.3.text: (2) When a single person rears a hundred heads (rúpasatam) made up of equal numbers of each of aged cows, milch cows, pregnant cows, heifers, and calves (vatsatari) and gives (to the owner) 8 várakas of clarified butter per annum, as well as the branded skin (of dead cows if any), that system is called ‘herds surrendered for a fixed amount of dairy produce.’
AS-2.29.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 3 (AS-2.29.3)

AS-2.29.30.text: Once in six months, sheep and other animals shall be shorn of their wool.
AS-2.29.30.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 30 (AS-2.29.30)

AS-2.29.31.text: The same rules shall apply to herds of horses, asses, camels, and hogs.
AS-2.29.31.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 31 (AS-2.29.31)

AS-2.29.32.text: For bulls which are provided with nose-rings, and which equal horses in speed and in carrying loads, half a bhára of meadow grass (yavasa), twice the above quantity of ordinary grass (trina), one tulá (100 palas) of oil cakes, 10 ádhakas of bran, 5 palas of salt (mukhalavanam), one kudumba of oil for rubbing over the nose (nasya), 1 prastha of drink (pána), one tulá of flesh, 1 ádhaka of curis, 1 drona of barley or of cooked másha (Phraseolus Radiatus), 1 drona of milk; or half an ádhaka of surá (liquor), 1 prastha of oil or ghi (sneha) 10 palas of sugar or jaggery, 1 pala of the fruit of sringibera (ginger) may be substituted for milk (pratipána).
AS-2.29.32.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 32 (AS-2.29.32)

AS-2.29.33.text: The same commodities less by one quarter each will form the diet for mules, cows, and asses; twice the quantity of the above things for buffaloes and camels.
AS-2.29.33.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 33 (AS-2.29.33)

AS-2.29.34.text: Draught oxen and cows, supplying milk (payah), shall be provided with subsistence in proportion to the duration of time the oxen are kept at work, and the quantity of milk which the cows supply.
AS-2.29.34.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 34 (AS-2.29.34)

AS-2.29.35.text: All cattle shall be supplied with abundance of fodder and water.
AS-2.29.35.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 35 (AS-2.29.35)

AS-2.29.36.text: Thus the manner of rearing herds of cattle has been dealt with.
AS-2.29.36.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 36 (AS-2.29.36)

AS-2.29.37.text: A herd of 100 heads of asses and mules shall contain 5 male animals; that of goats and sheep ten; and a herd of ten heads of either cows or buffaloes shall contain four male animals.
AS-2.29.37.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 37 (AS-2.29.37)

AS-2.29.4.text: (3) When those who rear a hundred heads made up of equal numbers of each of afflicted cattle, crippled cattle, cattle that cannot be milked by any one but the accustomed person, cattle that are not easily milked, and cattle that kill their own calves give in return (to the owner) a share in dairy produce, it is termed ‘useless and abandoned herd.’
AS-2.29.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 4 (AS-2.29.4)

AS-2.29.5.text: (4) When under the fear of cattle-lifting enemies (parachakrátavibhayát), cattle are kept under the care of the superintendent, giving him 1/10th of the dairy produce for his protection, it is termed "herds maintained for a share in dairy produce."
AS-2.29.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 5 (AS-2.29.5)

AS-2.29.6.text: (5) When the superintendent classifies cattle as calves, steers, tameable ones, draught oxen, bulls that are to be trained to yoke, bulls kept for crossing cows, cattle that are fit only for the supply of flesh, buffaloes and draught buffaloes; female calves, female steer, heifer, pregnant cows, milch cattle, barren cattle---either cows or buffaloes; calves that are a month or two old as well as those which are still younger; and when, as he ought to, he brands them all inclusive of their calves of one or two months old along with those stray cattle which have remained unclaimed in the herds for a month or two; and when he registers the branded marks, natural marks, colour and the distance from one horn to another of each of the cattle, that system is known as ‘class of herds.’
AS-2.29.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 6 (AS-2.29.6)

AS-2.29.7.text: (6) When an animal is carried off by thieves or finds itself into the herds of others or strays unknown, it is called ‘lost.’
AS-2.29.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 7 (AS-2.29.7)

AS-2.29.8.text: (7) When an animal is entangled in a quagmire or precipice or dies of disease or of old age, or drowned in water: or when it is killed by the fall of a tree or of river bank, or is beaten to death with a staff or stone, or is struck by lightening (ísána), or is devoured by a tiger or bitten by a cobra, or is carried off by a crocodile, or is involved in the midst of a forest fire, it is termed as “irrecoverably lost.”
AS-2.29.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 8 (AS-2.29.8)

AS-2.29.9.text: Cowherds shall endeavour to keep them away from such dangers.
AS-2.29.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 29, Sutra 9 (AS-2.29.9)

AS-2.3.1.text: ON all the four quarters of the boundaries of the kingdom, defensive fortifications against an enemy in war shall be constructed on grounds best fitted for the purpose: a water-fortification (audaka) such as an island in the midst of a river, or a plain surrounded by low ground; a mountainous fortification (párvata) such as a rocky tract or a cave; a desert (dhánvana) such as a wild tract devoid of water and overgrown with thicket growing in barren soil; or a forest fortification (vanadurga) full of wagtail (khajana), water and thickets.
AS-2.3.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 1 (AS-2.3.1)

AS-2.3.10.text: Between the tower and the broad street there shall be constructed an Indrakósa which is made up of covering pieces of wooden planks affording seats for three archers.
AS-2.3.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 10 (AS-2.3.10)

AS-2.3.11.text: There shall also be made a road for Gods which shall measure two hastas inside (the towers ?), four times as much by the sides, and eight hastas along the parapet.
AS-2.3.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 11 (AS-2.3.11)

AS-2.3.12.text: Paths (chárya, to ascend the parapet ?) as broad as a danda (6 ft.) or two shall also be made.
AS-2.3.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 12 (AS-2.3.12)

AS-2.3.13.text: In an unassailable part (of the rampart), a passage for flight (pradhávitikám), and a door for exit (nishkuradwáram) shall be made.
AS-2.3.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 13 (AS-2.3.13)

AS-2.3.14.text: Outside the rampart, passages for movements shall be closed by forming obstructions such as a knee-breaker (jánubhanjaní), a trident, mounds of earth, pits, wreaths of thorns, instruments made like the tail of a snake, palm leaf, triangle, and of dog's teeth, rods, ditches filled with thorns and covered with sand, frying pans and water-pools.
AS-2.3.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 14 (AS-2.3.14)

AS-2.3.15.text: Having made on both sides of the rampart a circular hole of a danda-and-a-half in diametre, an entrance gate (to the fort) one-sixth as broad as the width of the street shall be fixed.
AS-2.3.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 15 (AS-2.3.15)

AS-2.3.16.text: A square (chaturásra) is formed by successive addition of one danda up to eight dandas commencing from five, or in the proportion, one-sixth of the length up to one-eighth.
AS-2.3.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 16 (AS-2.3.16)

AS-2.3.17.text: The rise in level (talotsedhah) shall be made by successive addition of one hasta up to 18 hastas commencing from 15 hastas.
AS-2.3.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 17 (AS-2.3.17)

AS-2.3.18.text: In fixing a pillar, six parts are to form its height, on the floor, twice as much (12 parts) to be entered into the ground, and one-fourth for its capital.
AS-2.3.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 18 (AS-2.3.18)

AS-2.3.19.text: Of the first floor, five parts (are to be taken) for the formation of a hall (sálá), a well, and a boundary-house; two-tenths of it for the formation of two platforms opposite to each other (pratimanchau); an upper storey twice as high as its width; carvings of images; an upper-most storey, half or three-fourths as broad as the first floor; side walls built of bricks; on the left side, a staircase circumambulating from left to right; on the right, a secret staircase hidden in the wall; a top-support of ornamental arches (toranasirah) projecting as far as two hastas; two door-panels, (each) occupying three-fourths of the space; two and two cross-bars (parigha, to fasten the door); an iron-bolt (indrakila) as long as an aratni (24 angulas); a boundary gate (ánidváram) five hastas in width; four beams to shut the door against elephants;
AS-2.3.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 19 (AS-2.3.19)

AS-2.3.2.text: Of these, water and mountain fortifications are best suited to defend populous centres; and desert and forest fortifications are habitations in wilderness (atavísthánam).
AS-2.3.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 2 (AS-2.3.2)

AS-2.3.20.text: and turrets (hastinakha) (outside the rampart) raised up to the height of the face of a man, removable or irremovable, or made of earth in places devoid of water.
AS-2.3.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 20 (AS-2.3.20)

AS-2.3.21.text: A turret above the gate and starting from the top of the parapet shall be constructed, its front resembling an alligator up to three-fourths of its height.
AS-2.3.21.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 21 (AS-2.3.21)

AS-2.3.22.text: In the centre of the parapets, there shall be constructed a deep lotus pool; a rectangular building of four compartments, one within the other; an abode of the Goddess Kumiri (Kumárípuram), having its external area one-and-a-half times as broad as that of its innermost room; a circular building with an arch way; and in accordance with available space and materials, there shall also be constructed canals (kulyá) to hold weapons and three times as long as broad.
AS-2.3.22.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 22 (AS-2.3.22)

AS-2.3.23.text: In those canals, there shall be collected stones, spades (kuddála), axes (kuthári), varieties of staffs, cudgel (musrinthi), hammers (mudgara), clubs, discus, machines (yantra), and such weapons as can destroy a hundred persons at once (sataghni), together with spears, tridents, bamboo-sticks with pointed edges made of iron, camel-necks, explosives (agnisamyógas), and whatever else can be devised and formed from available materials.
AS-2.3.23.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 23 (AS-2.3.23)
