AS-2.3.3.text: Or with ready preparations for flight the king may have his fortified capital (stháníya) as the seat of his sovereignty (samudayásthánam) in the centre of his kingdom: in a locality naturally best fitted for the purpose, such as the bank of the confluence of rivers, a deep pool of perennial water, or of a lake or tank, a fort, circular, rectangular, or square in form, surrounded with an artificial canal of water, and connected with both land and water paths (may be constructed).
AS-2.3.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 3 (AS-2.3.3)

AS-2.3.4.text: Round this fort, three ditches with an intermediate space of one danda (6 ft.) from each other, fourteen, twelve and ten dandas respectively in width, with depth less by one quarter or by one-half of their width, square at their bottom and one-third as wide as at their top, with sides built of stones or bricks, filled with perennial flowing water or with water drawn from some other source, and possessing crocodiles and lotus plants shall be constructed.
AS-2.3.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 4 (AS-2.3.4)

AS-2.3.5.text: At a distance of four dandas (24 ft.) from the (innermost) ditch, a rampart six dandas high and twice as much broad shall be erected by heaping mud upwards and by making it square at the bottom, oval at the centre pressed by the trampling of elephants and bulls, and planted with thorny and poisonous plants in bushes. Gaps in the rampart shall be filled up with fresh earth.
AS-2.3.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 5 (AS-2.3.5)

AS-2.3.6.text: Above the rampart, parapets in odd or even numbers and with an intermediate, space of from 12 to 24 hastas from each other shall be built of bricks and raised to a height of twice their breadth.
AS-2.3.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 6 (AS-2.3.6)

AS-2.3.7.text: The passage for chariots shall be made of trunks of palm trees or of broad and thick slabs of stones with spheres like the head of a monkey carved on their surface; but never of wood as fire finds a happy abode in it.
AS-2.3.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 7 (AS-2.3.7)

AS-2.3.8.text: Towers, square throughout and with moveable staircase or ladder equal to its height, shall also be constructed.
AS-2.3.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 8 (AS-2.3.8)

AS-2.3.9.text: In the intermediate space measuring thirty dandas between two towers, there shall be formed a broad street in two compartments covered over with a roof and two-and- half times as long as it is broad.
AS-2.3.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 3, Sutra 9 (AS-2.3.9)

AS-2.30.1.text: THE Superintendent of Horses shall register the breed, age, colour, marks, group or classes, and the native place of horses, and classify as (1) those that are kept in sale-house for sale (panyágárikam), (2) those that are recently purchased (krayopágatam), (3) those that have been captured in wars (áhavalabdham), (4) those that are of local breed (ájátam), (5) those that are sent thither for help (sáháyyakágatam), (6) those that are mortgaged (panasthitam), and (7) those that are temporarily kept in stables (yávatkálikam).
AS-2.30.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 1 (AS-2.30.1)

AS-2.30.10.text: For the best horse (the diet shall be) 2 dronas of any one of the grains, rice (sáli, vríhi,) barley, panic seeds (priyangu) soaked or cooked, cooked mudga (Phraseolus Munga) or másha (Phraseolus Radiatus); one prastha of oil, 5 palas of salt, 50 palas of flesh, 1 ádhaka of broth (rasa) or 2 ádhakas of curd, 5 palas of sugar (kshára), to make their diet relishing, 1 prastha of súrá, liquor, or 2 prasthas of milk.
AS-2.30.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 10 (AS-2.30.10)

AS-2.30.11.text: The same quantity of drink shall be specially given to those horses which are tired of long journey or of carrying loads.
AS-2.30.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 11 (AS-2.30.11)

AS-2.30.12.text: One prastha of oil for giving enema (anuvásana), 1 kudumba of oil for rubbing over the nose, 1,000 palas of meadow grass, twice as much of ordinary grass (trina); and hay-stalk or grass shall be spread over an area of 6 aratnis.
AS-2.30.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 12 (AS-2.30.12)

AS-2.30.13.text: The same quantity of rations less by one-quarter for horses of medium and lower size.
AS-2.30.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 13 (AS-2.30.13)

AS-2.30.14.text: A draught horse or stallion of medium size shall be given the same quantity as the best horse; and similar horses of lower size shall receive the same quantity as a horse of medium size.
AS-2.30.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 14 (AS-2.30.14)

AS-2.30.15.text: Steeds and párasamas shall have one quarter less of rations.
AS-2.30.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 15 (AS-2.30.15)

AS-2.30.16.text: Half of the rations given to steeds shall be given to colts.
AS-2.30.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 16 (AS-2.30.16)

AS-2.30.17.text: Those who cook the food of horses, grooms, and veterinary surgeons shall have a share in the rations (pratisvádabhajah).
AS-2.30.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 17 (AS-2.30.17)

AS-2.30.18.text: Stallions which are incapacitated owing to old age, disease or hardships of war, and, being therefore rendered unfit for use in war live only to consume food shall in the interests of citizens and country people be allowed to cross steeds.
AS-2.30.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 18 (AS-2.30.18)

AS-2.30.19.text: The breed of Kámbhoja, Sindhu, Aratta, and Vanáyu countries are the best; those of Báhlíka, Pápeya, Sauvira, and Taitala, are of middle quality; and the rest ordinary (avaráh).
AS-2.30.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 19 (AS-2.30.19)

AS-2.30.2.text: He shall make a report (to the king) of such animals as are inauspicious, crippled, or diseased.
AS-2.30.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 2 (AS-2.30.2)

AS-2.30.20.text: These three sorts may be trained either for war or for riding according as they are furious (tíkshna), mild (bhadra), or stupid or slow (manda).
AS-2.30.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 20 (AS-2.30.20)

AS-2.30.21.text: The regular training of a horse is its preparation for war (sánnáhyam karma).
AS-2.30.21.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 21 (AS-2.30.21)

AS-2.30.22.text: Circular movement (valgana), slow movement (níchairgata), jumping (langhana), gallop (dhorana), and response to signals (nároshtra) are the several forms of riding (aupaváhya).
AS-2.30.22.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 22 (AS-2.30.22)

AS-2.30.23.text: Aupavenuka, vardhmánaka, yamaka, álídhapluta, vrithatta and trivacháli are the varieties of circular movement (valgana).
AS-2.30.23.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 23 (AS-2.30.23)

AS-2.30.24.text: The same kind of movements with the head and ear kept erect are called slow movements.
AS-2.30.24.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 24 (AS-2.30.24)

AS-2.30.25.text: Prakírnaka, prakírnottara, nishanna, pársvánuvritta, úrmimárga, sarabhakrídita, sarabhapluta, tritála, báhyánuvritta, panchapáni, simháyata, svádhúta, klishta, slághita, brimhita, pushpábhikírna.
AS-2.30.25.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 25 (AS-2.30.25)

AS-2.30.26.text: Jumping like a monkey (kapipluta), jumping like a frog (bhekapluta), sudden jump (ekapluta), jumping with one leg (ekapádapluta), leaping like a cuckoo (kokila-samchári), dashing with its breast almost touching the ground (urasya), and leaping like a crane (bakasamchari) are the several forms of jumping.
AS-2.30.26.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 26 (AS-2.30.26)

AS-2.30.27.text: Flying like a vulture (kánka), dashing like a water-duck (várikánaka), running like a peacock (máyúra) halt the speed of a peacock (ardhmáyúra), dashing like a mangoose (nákula), half the speed of a mangoose (ardha-nákula), running like a hog (váráha) and half the speed of a hog (ardha- váráha) are the several forms of gallop.
AS-2.30.27.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 27 (AS-2.30.27)

AS-2.30.28.text: Six, nine, and twelve yojanas (a day) are the distances (to be traversed) by carriage-horses.
AS-2.30.28.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 28 (AS-2.30.28)

AS-2.30.29.text: Five, eight, and ten yojanas are the distances (to be traversed) by riding horses (prishthaváhya).
AS-2.30.29.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 29 (AS-2.30.29)

AS-2.30.3.text: Every horseman shall know how to make an economic use of whatever he has received from the king's treasury and storehouse.
AS-2.30.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 3 (AS-2.30.3)

AS-2.30.30.text: Trotting according to its strength (vikrama), trotting with good breathing (bhadrásvása), and pacing with a load on its back are the three kinds of trot.
AS-2.30.30.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 30 (AS-2.30.30)

AS-2.30.31.text: Trotting according to strength (vikrama), trot combined with circular movement (valgita), ordinary trot (upakantha), middlemost speed (upajava), and ordinary speed are also the several kinds of trot (dhárá).
AS-2.30.31.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 31 (AS-2.30.31)

AS-2.30.32.text: Qualified teachers shall give instructions as to the manufacture of proper ropes with which to tether the horses.
AS-2.30.32.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 32 (AS-2.30.32)

AS-2.30.33.text: Charioteers shall see to the manufacture of necessary war accoutrements of horses.
AS-2.30.33.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 33 (AS-2.30.33)

AS-2.30.34.text: Veterinary surgeons shall apply requisite remedies against undue growth or diminution in the body of horses and also change the diet of horses according to changes in seasons.
AS-2.30.34.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 34 (AS-2.30.34)

AS-2.30.35.text: Those who move the horses (sútragráhaka), those whose business is to tether them in stables, those who supply meadow-grass, those who cook the grains for the horses, those who keep watch in the stables, those who groom them and those who apply remedies against poison shall satisfactorily discharge their specified duties and shall, in default of it, forfeit their daily wages.
AS-2.30.35.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 35 (AS-2.30.35)

AS-2.30.36.text: Those who take out for the purpose of riding such horses as are kept inside (the stables) either for the purpose of waving lights (nirájana) or for medical treatment shall be fined 12 panas.
AS-2.30.36.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 36 (AS-2.30.36)

AS-2.30.37.text: When, owing to defects in medicine or carelessness in the treatment, the disease (from which a horse is suffering) becomes intense, a fine of twice the cost of the treatment shall be imposed; and when, owing to defects in medicine, or not administering it, the result becomes quite the reverse, a fine equal to the value of the animal (patramúlya) shall be imposed.
AS-2.30.37.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 37 (AS-2.30.37)

AS-2.30.38.text: The same rule shall apply to the treatment of cows, buffaloes, goats, and sheep.
AS-2.30.38.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 38 (AS-2.30.38)

AS-2.30.39.text: Horses shall be washed, bedaubed with sandal powder, and garlanded twice a day. On new moon days sacrifice to Bhútas, and on full moon days the chanting of auspicious hymns shall be performed. Not only on the ninth day of the month of Asvayuja, but also both at the commencement and close of journeys (yátra) as well as in the time of disease shall a priest wave lights invoking blessings on the horses.
AS-2.30.39.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 39 (AS-2.30.39)

AS-2.30.4.text: The superintendent shall have a stable constructed as spacious as required by the number of horses to be kept therein twice as broad as the length of a horse, with four doors facing the four quarters, with its central floor suited for the rolling of horses, with projected front provided with wooden seats at the entrance, and containing monkeys, peacocks, red spotted deer (prishata), mangoose, partridges (chakora), parrots, and maina birds (sárika); the room for every horse shall be four times as broad or long as the length of a horse, with its central floor paved with smoothened wooden planks, with separate compartments for fodder (khádanakoshthakam), with passages for the removal of urine and dung, and with a door facing either the north or the east. The distinction of quarters (digvibhága) may be made as a matter of fact or relatively to the situation of the building.
AS-2.30.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 4 (AS-2.30.4)

AS-2.30.5.text: A steed that has just given birth to a colt shall be provided for the first three days with a drink of 1 prastha of clarified butter; afterwards it shall be fed with a prastha of flour (saktu) and made to drink oil mixed with medicine for ten nights; after that time, it shall have cooked grains, meadow grass, and other things suited to the season of the day.
AS-2.30.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 5 (AS-2.30.5)

AS-2.30.6.text: A colt, ten days old, shall be given a kudumba of flour mixed with ¼th kudumba of clarified butter, and 1 prastha of milk till it becomes six months old; then the above rations shall be increased half as much during each succeeding month, with the addition of 1 prastha of barley till it becomes three years old, then one drona of barley till it grows four years old; at the age of four or five, it attains its full development and becomes serviceable.
AS-2.30.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 6 (AS-2.30.6)

AS-2.30.7.text: The face (mukha) of the best horse measures 32 angulas; its length is 5 times its face; its shank is 20 angulas; and its height is 4 times its shank.
AS-2.30.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 7 (AS-2.30.7)

AS-2.30.8.text: Horses of medium and lower sizes fall short of the above measurement by two and three angulas respectively.
AS-2.30.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 8 (AS-2.30.8)

AS-2.30.9.text: The circumference (parínáha) of the best horse measures 100 angulas, and horses of medium and lower sizes fall short of the above measurement by five parts (panchabhágávaram).
AS-2.30.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 30, Sutra 9 (AS-2.30.9)

AS-2.31.1.text: THE Superintendent of elephants shall take proper steps to protect elephant-forests and supervise the operations with regard to the standing or lying in stables of elephants, male, female, or young, when they are tired after training, and examine the proportional quantity of rations and grass, the extent of training given to them, their accoutrements and ornaments, as well as the work of elephant-doctors, of trainers of elephants in warlike feats, and of grooms, such as drivers, binders and others.
AS-2.31.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 1 (AS-2.31.1)

AS-2.31.10.text: The diet (for the last two classes) shall be lessened by one-quarter according to the class.
AS-2.31.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 10 (AS-2.31.10)

AS-2.31.11.text: The rations for an elephant (of seven aratnis in height) shall be 1 drona of rice, ½ ádhaka of oil, 3 prasthas of ghi, 10 palas of salt, 50 palas of flesh, 1 ádhaka of broth (rasa) or twice the quantity (i.e., 2 ádhakas) of curd; in order to render the dish tasteful, 10 palas of sugar (kshára), 1 ádhaka of liquor, or twice the quantity of milk (payah) ; 1 prastha of oil for smearing over the body, 1/8 prastha (of the same) for the head and for keeping a light in the stables; 2 bháras of meadow grass, 2¼ bháras of ordinary grass (sashpa), and 2½ bháras of dry grass and any quantity of stalks of various pulses (kadankara).
AS-2.31.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 11 (AS-2.31.11)

AS-2.31.12.text: An elephant in rut (atyarála) and of 8 aratnis in height shall have equal rations with that of 7 aratnis in height.
AS-2.31.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 12 (AS-2.31.12)

AS-2.31.13.text: The rest of 6 or 5 aratnis in height shall be provided with rations proportional to their size.
AS-2.31.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 13 (AS-2.31.13)

AS-2.31.14.text: A young elephant (bikka) captured for the mere purpose of sporting with it shall be fed with milk and meadow grass.
AS-2.31.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 14 (AS-2.31.14)

AS-2.31.15.text: That which is blood-red (samjátalóhita), that which is fleshed, that which has its sides evenly grown (samaliptapakshá), that which has its girths full or equal (samakakshyá), that whose flesh is evenly spread, that which is of even surface on its back (samatalpatala) and that which is of uneven surface (játadróniká) are the several kinds of physical splendour of elephants.
AS-2.31.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 15 (AS-2.31.15)

AS-2.31.16.text: Suitably to the seasons as well as to their physical spendour, elephants of sharp or slow sense (bhadra and mandra) as well as elephants possessed of the characteristics of other beasts shall be trained and taught suitable work.
AS-2.31.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 16 (AS-2.31.16)

AS-2.31.2.text: There shall be constructed an elephant stable twice as broad and twice as high as the length (áyáma) of an elephant, with separate apartments for female elephants, with projected entrance (sapragrívám), with posts called kumári, and with its door facing either the east or the north.
AS-2.31.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 2 (AS-2.31.2)

AS-2.31.3.text: The space in front of the smooth posts (to which elephants are tied) shall form a square, one side of which is equal to the length of an elephant and shall be paved with smooth wooden planks and provided with holes for the removal of urine and dung.
AS-2.31.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 3 (AS-2.31.3)

AS-2.31.4.text: The space where an elephant lies down shall be as broad as the length of an elephant and provided with a flat form raised to half the height of an elephant for leaning on.
AS-2.31.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 4 (AS-2.31.4)

AS-2.31.5.text: Elephants serviceable in war or for riding shall be kept inside the fort; and those that are still being tamed or are of bad temper shall be kept outside.
AS-2.31.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 5 (AS-2.31.5)

AS-2.31.6.text: The first and the seventh of the eight divisions of the day are the two bathing times of elephants; the time subsequent to those two periods is for their food; forenoon is the time for their exercise; afternoon is the time for drink; two (out of eight) parts of the night are the time for sleep; one-third of the night is spent in taking wakeful rest.
AS-2.31.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 6 (AS-2.31.6)

AS-2.31.7.text: Young elephants (bikka), infatuated elephants (mugdha), elephants without tusks, diseased elephants, elephants which suckle their young ones (dhenuká), and female elephants (hastiní) shall not be captured.
AS-2.31.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 7 (AS-2.31.7)

AS-2.31.8.text: (That which is) seven aratnis in height, nine aratnis in length, ten aratnis in circumference and is (as can be inferred from such measurement), 40 years old, is the best.
AS-2.31.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 8 (AS-2.31.8)

AS-2.31.9.text: That which is 30 years old is of middle class; and that which is 25 years old is of the lowest class.
AS-2.31.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 31, Sutra 9 (AS-2.31.9)

AS-2.32.1.text: ELEPHANTS are classified into four kinds in accordance with the training they are given: that which is tameable (damya), that which is trained for war (sánnáhya), that which is trained for riding (aupaváhya), and rogue elephants (vyála).
AS-2.32.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 1 (AS-2.32.1)

AS-2.32.10.text: The form of fetters and other necessary means to keep them under control shall be ascertained from the doctor of elephants.
AS-2.32.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 10 (AS-2.32.10)

AS-2.32.11.text: Tetherposts (álána), collars, girths, bridles, legchains, frontal fetters are the several kinds of binding instruments.
AS-2.32.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 11 (AS-2.32.11)

AS-2.32.12.text: A hook, a bamboo staff, and machines (yantra) are instruments.
AS-2.32.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 12 (AS-2.32.12)

AS-2.32.13.text: Necklaces such as vaijavantí and kshurapramála, and litter and housings are the ornaments of elephants.
AS-2.32.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 13 (AS-2.32.13)

AS-2.32.14.text: Mail-armour (varma), clubs (totra), arrow-bags, and machines are war-accoutrements.
AS-2.32.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 14 (AS-2.32.14)

AS-2.32.15.text: Elephant doctors, trainers, expert riders, as well as those who groom them, those who prepare their food, those who procure grass for them, those who tether them to posts, those who sweep elephant stables, and those who keep watch in the stables at night, are some of the persons that have to attend to the needs of elephants.
AS-2.32.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 15 (AS-2.32.15)

AS-2.32.16.text: Elephant doctors, watchmen, sweepers, cooks and others shall receive (from the storehouse,) 1 prastha of cooked rice, a handful of oil, land 2 palas of sugar and of salt. Excepting the doctors, others shall also receive 10 palas of flesh.
AS-2.32.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 16 (AS-2.32.16)

AS-2.32.17.text: Elephant doctors shall apply necessary medicines to elephants which, while making a journey, happen to suffer from disease, overwork, rut, or old age.
AS-2.32.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 17 (AS-2.32.17)

AS-2.32.18.text: Accumulation of dirt in stables, failure to supply grass, causing an elephant to lie down on hard and unprepared ground, striking on vital parts of its body, permission to a stranger to ride over it, untimely riding, leading it to water through impassable places, and allowing it to enter into thick forests are offences punishable with fines. Such fines shall be deducted from the rations and wages due to the offenders.
AS-2.32.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 18 (AS-2.32.18)

AS-2.32.19.text: During the period of Cháturmásya (the months of July, August, September and October) and at the time when two seasons meet, waving of lights shall be performed thrice. Also on new-moon and full-moon days, commanders shall perform sacrifices to Bhútas for the safety of elephants.
AS-2.32.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 19 (AS-2.32.19)

AS-2.32.2.text: Those which are tameable fall under five groups: that which suffers a man to sit on its withers (skandhagata), that which allows itself to be tethered to a post (stambhagata), that which can be taken to water (várigata), that which lies in pits (apapátagata), and that which is attached to its herd (yúthagata).
AS-2.32.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 2 (AS-2.32.2)

AS-2.32.20.text: Leaving as much as is equal to twice the circumference of the tusk near its root, the rest of the tusks shall be cut off once in 2½ years in the case of elephants born in countries irrigated by rivers (nadija), and once in 5 years in the case of mountain elephants.
AS-2.32.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 20 (AS-2.32.20)

AS-2.32.3.text: All these elephants shall be treated with as much care as a young elephant (bikka).
AS-2.32.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 3 (AS-2.32.3)

AS-2.32.4.text: Military training is of seven kinds: Drill (upasthána), turning (samvartana), advancing (samyána), trampling down and killing (vadhávadha), fighting with other elephants (hastiyuddha), assailing forts and cities (nágaráyanam), and warfare.
AS-2.32.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 4 (AS-2.32.4)

AS-2.32.5.text: Binding the elephants with girths (kakshyákarma), putting on collars (graiveyakakarma), and making them work in company with their herds (yúthakarma) are the first steps (upa-vichara) of the above training.
AS-2.32.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 5 (AS-2.32.5)

AS-2.32.6.text: Elephants trained for riding fall under seven groups: that which suffers a man to mount over it when in company with another elephant (kunjaropaváhya), that which suffers riding when led by a warlike elephant (sánnáhyopaváhya), that which is taught trotting (dhorana), that which is taught various kinds of movements (ádhánagatika), that which can be made to move by using a staff (yashtyupaváhya), that which can be made to move by using an iron hook (totropaváhya), that which can be made to move without whips (suddhopaváhya), and that which is of help in hunting.
AS-2.32.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 6 (AS-2.32.6)

AS-2.32.7.text: Autumnal work (sáradakarma), mean or rough work (hínakarma), and training to respond to signals are the first steps for the above training.
AS-2.32.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 7 (AS-2.32.7)

AS-2.32.8.text: Rogue elephants can be trained only in one way. The only means to keep them under control is punishment. It has a suspicious aversion to work, is obstinate, of perverse nature, unsteady, willful, or of infatuated temper under the influence of rut.
AS-2.32.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 8 (AS-2.32.8)

AS-2.32.9.text: Rogue elephants whose training proves a failure may be purely roguish (suddha), clever in roguery (suvrata), perverse (vishama), or possessed of all kinds of vice.
AS-2.32.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 32, Sutra 9 (AS-2.32.9)

AS-2.33.1.text: THE functions of the Superintendent of horses will explain those of the Superintendent of chariots.
AS-2.33.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 33, Sutra 1 (AS-2.33.1)

AS-2.33.10.text: With an eye to the position which the entire army (chaturangabala) trained in the skillful handling of all kinds of weapons and in leading elephants, horses, and chariots have occupied and to the emergent call for which they ought to be ready, the commander-in-chief shall be so capable as to order either advance or retreat (áyogamayógam cha).
AS-2.33.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 33, Sutra 10 (AS-2.33.10)

AS-2.33.11.text: He shall also know what kind of ground is more advantageous to his own army, what time is more favourable, what the strength of the enemy is, how to sow dissension in an enemy's army of united mind, how to collect his own scattered forces, how to scatter the compact body of an enemy's army, how to assail a fortress, and when to make a general advance.
AS-2.33.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 33, Sutra 11 (AS-2.33.11)

AS-2.33.12.text: Being ever mindful of the discipline which his army has to maintain not merely in camping and marching, but in the thick of battle, he shall designate the regiments (vyúha) by the names of trumpets, boards, banners, or flags.
AS-2.33.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 33, Sutra 12 (AS-2.33.12)

AS-2.33.2.text: The Superintendent of chariots shall attend to the construction of chariots.
AS-2.33.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 33, Sutra 2 (AS-2.33.2)

AS-2.33.3.text: The best chariot shall measure 10 purushas in height (,i.e., 120 angulas), and 12 purushas in width. After this model, 7 more chariots with width decreasing by one purusha successively down to a chariot of 6 purushas in width shall be constructed. He shall also construct chariots of gods (devaratha), festal chariots (pushyaratha), battle chariots (sángrámika), travelling chariots (páriyánika), chariots used in assailing an enemy's strong-holds (parapurabhiyánika), and training chariots.
AS-2.33.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 33, Sutra 3 (AS-2.33.3)

AS-2.33.4.text: He shall also examine the efficiency in the training of troops in shooting arrows, in hurling clubs and cudgels, in wearing mail armour, in equipment, in charioteering, in fighting seated on a chariot, and in controlling chariot horses.
AS-2.33.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 33, Sutra 4 (AS-2.33.4)

AS-2.33.5.text: He shall also attend to the accounts of provision and wages paid to those who are either permanently or temporarily employed (to prepare chariots and other things). Also he shall take steps to maintain the employed contented and happy by adequate reward (yogyarakshanushthánam), and ascertain the distance of roads.
AS-2.33.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 33, Sutra 5 (AS-2.33.5)

AS-2.33.6.text: The same rules shall apply to the superintendent of infantry.
AS-2.33.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 33, Sutra 6 (AS-2.33.6)

AS-2.33.7.text: The latter shall know the exact strength or weakness of hereditary troops (maula), hired troops (bhrita), the corporate body of troops (sreni), as well as that of the army of friendly or unfriendly kings and of wild tribes.
AS-2.33.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 33, Sutra 7 (AS-2.33.7)

AS-2.33.8.text: He shall be thoroughly familiar with the nature of fighting in low grounds, of open battle, of fraudulent attack, of fighting under the cover of entrenchment (khanakayuddha), or from heights (ákásayuddha), and of fighting during the day and night, besides the drill necessary for such warfare.
AS-2.33.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 33, Sutra 8 (AS-2.33.8)

AS-2.33.9.text: He shall also know the fitness or unfitness of troops on emergent occasions.
AS-2.33.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 33, Sutra 9 (AS-2.33.9)

AS-2.34.1.text: THE Superintendent of Passports shall issue passes at the rate of a masha per pass. Whoever is provided with a pass shall be at liberty to enter into, or go out of, the country. Whoever, being a native of the country enters into or goes out of the country without a pass shall be fined 12 panas. He shall be punished with the first amercement for producing a false pass. A foreigner guilty of the same offence shall be punished with the highest amercement.
AS-2.34.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 34, Sutra 1 (AS-2.34.1)

AS-2.34.2.text: Pasture grounds shall be opened between any two dangerous places.
AS-2.34.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 34, Sutra 2 (AS-2.34.2)

AS-2.34.3.text: Valleys shall be cleared from the fear of thieves, elephants, and other beasts.
AS-2.34.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 34, Sutra 3 (AS-2.34.3)

AS-2.34.4.text: In barren tracts of the country, there shall be constructed not only tanks, buildings for shelter, and wells, but also flower gardens and fruit gardens.
AS-2.34.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 34, Sutra 4 (AS-2.34.4)

AS-2.34.5.text: Hunters with their hounds shall reconnoitre forests. At the approach of thieves or enemies, they shall so hide themselves by ascending trees or mountains as to escape from the thieves, and blow conch-shells or beat drums. As to the movements of enemies or wild tribes, they may send information by flying the pigeons of royal household with passes (mudrá) or causing fire and smoke at successive distances.
AS-2.34.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 34, Sutra 5 (AS-2.34.5)

AS-2.34.6.text: It shall be his duty to protect timber and elephant forests, to keep roads in good repair, to arrest thieves, to secure the safety of mercantile traffic, to protect cows, and to conduct the transaction of the people.
AS-2.34.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 34, Sutra 6 (AS-2.34.6)

AS-2.35.1.text: HAVING divided the kingdom (janapada) into four districts, and having also subdivided the villages (gráma) as of first, middle and lowest rank, he shall bring them under one or another of the following heads:---Villages that are exempted from taxation (pariháraka); those that supply soldiers (áyudhíya); those that pay their taxes in the form of grains, cattle, gold (hiranya), or raw material (kupya); and those that supply free labour (vishti), and dairy produce in lieu of taxes (karapratikara).
AS-2.35.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 1 (AS-2.35.1)

AS-2.35.10.text: They shall also find out the causes of emigration and immigration of persons of migratory habit, the arrival and departure of men and women of condemnable (anarthya) character, as well as the movements of (foreign) spies.
AS-2.35.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 10 (AS-2.35.10)

AS-2.35.11.text: Likewise spies under the guise of merchants shall ascertain the quantity and price of the royal merchandise such as minerals, or products of gardens, forests, and fields or manufactured articles.
AS-2.35.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 11 (AS-2.35.11)

AS-2.35.12.text: As regards foreign merchandise of superior or inferior quality arriving thither by land or by water, they shall ascertain the amount of toll, road-cess, conveyance-cess, military cess, ferry-fare, and one-sixth portion (paid or payable by the merchants), the charges incurred by them for their own subsistence, and for the accommodation of their merchandise in warehouse (panyágára).
AS-2.35.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 12 (AS-2.35.12)

AS-2.35.13.text: Similarly spies under the guise of ascetics shall, as ordered by the Collector-general, gather information as to the proceedings, honest or dishonest, of cultivators, cow-herds, merchants, and heads of Government departments.
AS-2.35.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 13 (AS-2.35.13)

AS-2.35.14.text: In places where altars are situated or where four roads meet, in ancient ruins, in the vicinity of tanks, rivers, bathing places, in places of pilgrimage and hermitage, and in desert tracts, mountains, and thick grown forests, spies under the guise of old and notorious thieves with their student bands shall ascertain the causes of arrival and departure, and halt of thieves, enemies, and persons of undue bravery.
AS-2.35.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 14 (AS-2.35.14)

AS-2.35.15.text: The Collector-general shall thus energetically attend to the affairs of the kingdom. Also his subordinates constituting his various establishments of espionage shall along with their colleagues and followers attend to their duties likewise.
AS-2.35.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 15 (AS-2.35.15)

AS-2.35.2.text: It is the duty of Gopa, village accountant, to attend to the accounts of five or ten villages as ordered by the Collector-General.
AS-2.35.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 2 (AS-2.35.2)

AS-2.35.3.text: By setting up boundaries to villages, by numbering plots of grounds as cultivated, uncultivated, plains, wet lands, gardens, vegetable gardens, fences (váta), forests, altars, temples of gods, irrigation works, cremation grounds, feeding houses (sattra), places where water is freely supplied to travellers (prapá), places of pilgrimage, pasture grounds and roads, and thereby fixing the boundaries of various villages, of fields, of forests, and of roads, he shall register gifts, sales, charities, and remission of taxes regarding fields.
AS-2.35.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 3 (AS-2.35.3)

AS-2.35.4.text: Also having numbered the houses as taxpaying or non-taxpaying, he shall not only register the total number of the inhabitants of all the four castes in each village, but also keep an account of the exact number of cultivators, cow-herds, merchants, artizans, labourers, slaves, and biped and quadruped animals, fixing at the same time the amount of gold, free labour, toll, and fines that can be collected from it (each house).
AS-2.35.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 4 (AS-2.35.4)

AS-2.35.5.text: He shall also keep an account of the number of young and old men that reside in each house, their history (charitra), occupation (ájíva), income (áya), and expenditure (vyaya).
AS-2.35.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 5 (AS-2.35.5)

AS-2.35.6.text: Likewise Sthánika, district officer, shall attend to the accounts of one quarter of the kingdom.
AS-2.35.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 6 (AS-2.35.6)

AS-2.35.7.text: In those places which are under the jurisdiction of Gopa and Sthánika, commissioners (prodeshtárah) specially deputed by the Collector-general shall not only inspect the work done and the means employed by the village and district officers, but also collect the special religious tax known as bali (balipragraham kuryuh).
AS-2.35.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 7 (AS-2.35.7)

AS-2.35.8.text: Spies under the disguise of householders (grihapatika, cultivators) who shall be deputed by the collector-general for espionage shall ascertain the validity of the accounts (of the village and district officers) regarding the fields, houses and families of each village---the area and output of produce regarding fields, right of ownership and remission of taxes with regard to houses, and the caste and profession regarding families.
AS-2.35.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 8 (AS-2.35.8)

AS-2.35.9.text: They shall also ascertain the total number of men and beasts (janghágra) as well as the amount of income and expenditure of each family.
AS-2.35.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 35, Sutra 9 (AS-2.35.9)

AS-2.36.1.text: LIKE the Collector-general, the Officer in charge of the Capital City (Nágaraka) shall look to the affairs of the capital.
AS-2.36.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 1 (AS-2.36.1)

AS-2.36.10.text: Any physician who undertakes to treat in secret a patient suffering from ulcer or excess of unwholesome food or drink, as well as the master of the house (wherein such treatment is attempted) shall be innocent only when they (the physician and the master of the house) make a report of the same to either Gopa or Sthánika; otherwise both of them shall be equally guilty with the sufferer.
AS-2.36.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 10 (AS-2.36.10)

AS-2.36.11.text: Masters of houses shall make a report of strangers arriving at, or departing from their houses; otherwise they shall be guilty of the offence (theft, etc.) committed during that night. Even during safe nights (i.e., nights when no theft, etc., seems to have been committed), they shall be fined 3 panas (for not making such a report).
AS-2.36.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 11 (AS-2.36.11)

AS-2.36.12.text: Wayfarers going along a high road or by a foot path shall catch hold of any person whom they find to be suffering from a wound or ulcer, or possessed of destructive instruments, or tired of carrying a heavy load, or timidly avoiding the presence of others, or indulging in too much sleep, or fatigued from a long journey, or who appears to be a stranger to the place in localities such as inside or outside the capital, temples of gods, places of pilgrimage, or burial grounds.
AS-2.36.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 12 (AS-2.36.12)

AS-2.36.13.text: (Spies) shall also make a search for suspicious persons in the interior of deserted houses, in the workshops or houses of vintners and sellers of cooked rice and flesh, in gambling houses, and in the abode of heretics.
AS-2.36.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 13 (AS-2.36.13)

AS-2.36.14.text: Kindling of fire shall be prohibited during the two middlemost parts of day-time divided into four equal parts during the summer. A fine of 1/8th of a pana shall be imposed for kindling fire at such a time.
AS-2.36.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 14 (AS-2.36.14)

AS-2.36.15.text: Masters of houses may carry on cooking operations outside their houses.
AS-2.36.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 15 (AS-2.36.15)

AS-2.36.16.text: (If a house-owner is not found to have ready with him) five water-pots (pancha ghatínám), a kumbha, a dróna, a ladder, an axe, a winnowing basket, a hook (such as is used to drive an elephant), pincers, (kachagráhini), and a leather bag (driti), he shall be fined ¼th of a pana.
AS-2.36.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 16 (AS-2.36.16)

AS-2.36.17.text: They shall also remove thatched roofs. Those who work by fire (blacksmiths) shall all together live in a single locality.
AS-2.36.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 17 (AS-2.36.17)

AS-2.36.18.text: Each houseowner shall ever be present (at night) at the door of his own house.
AS-2.36.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 18 (AS-2.36.18)

AS-2.36.19.text: Vessels filled with water shall be kept in thousands in a row without confusion not only in big streets and at places where four roads meet but also in front of the royal buildings (rajaprigraheshu).
AS-2.36.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 19 (AS-2.36.19)

AS-2.36.2.text: A Gopa shall keep the accounts of ten households, twenty households, or forty households. He shall not only know the caste, gotra, the name, and occupation of both men and women in those households, but also ascertain their income and expenditure.
AS-2.36.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 2 (AS-2.36.2)

AS-2.36.20.text: Any house-owner who does not run to give his help in extinguishing the fire of whatever is burning shall be fined 12 panas; and a renter (avakrayi, i.e., one who has occupied a house for rent) not running to extinguish fire shall be fined 6 panas.
AS-2.36.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 20 (AS-2.36.20)

AS-2.36.21.text: Whoever carelessly sets fire (to a house) shall be fined 54 panas; but he who intentionally sets fire (to a house) shall be thrown into fire.
AS-2.36.21.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 21 (AS-2.36.21)

AS-2.36.22.text: Whoever throws dirt in the street shall be punished with a fine of 1/8th of a pana; whoever causes mire or water to collect in the street shall be fined ¼th of a pana; whoever commits the above offences in the king's road (rájamárga) shall be punished with double the above fines.
AS-2.36.22.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 22 (AS-2.36.22)

AS-2.36.23.text: Whoever excretes faeces in places of pilgrimage, reservoirs of water, temples, and royal buildings shall be punished with fines rising from one pana and upwards in the order of the offences; but when such excretions are due to the use of medicine or to disease no punishment shall be imposed.
AS-2.36.23.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 23 (AS-2.36.23)

AS-2.36.24.text: Whoever throws inside the city the carcass of animals such as a cat, dog, mangoose, and a snake shall be fined 3 panas; of animals such as an ass, a camel, a mule, and cattle shall be fined 6 panas; and human corpse shall be punished with a fine of 50 panas.
AS-2.36.24.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 24 (AS-2.36.24)

AS-2.36.25.text: When a dead body is taken out of a city through a gate other than the usual or prescribed one or through a path other than the prescribed path, the first amercement shall be imposed; and those who guard the gates (through which the dead body is taken out) shall be fined 200 panas.
AS-2.36.25.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 25 (AS-2.36.25)

AS-2.36.26.text: When a dead body is interred or cremated beyond the burial or cremation grounds, a fine of 12 panas shall be imposed.
AS-2.36.26.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 26 (AS-2.36.26)

AS-2.36.27.text: The interval between six nálikas (2 2/5 hours) after the fall of night and six nálikas before the dawn shall be the period when a trumpet shall be sounded prohibiting the movement of the people.
AS-2.36.27.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 27 (AS-2.36.27)

AS-2.36.28.text: The trumpet having been sounded, whoever moves in the vicinity of royal buildings during the first or the last yáma (3 hours ?) of the period shall be punished with a fine of one pana and a quarter; and during the middlemost yámas, with double the above fine; and whoever moves outside (the royal buildings or the fort) shall be punished with four times the above fine.
AS-2.36.28.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 28 (AS-2.36.28)

AS-2.36.29.text: Whoever is arrested in suspicious places or as the perpetrator of a criminal act shall be examined.
AS-2.36.29.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 29 (AS-2.36.29)

AS-2.36.3.text: Likewise, the officer known as Sthánika shall attend to the accounts of the four quarters of the capital.
AS-2.36.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 3 (AS-2.36.3)

AS-2.36.30.text: Whoever moves in the vicinity of royal buildings or ascends the defensive fortifications of the capital shall be punished with the middlemost amercement.
AS-2.36.30.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 30 (AS-2.36.30)

AS-2.36.31.text: Those who go out at night in order to attend to the work of midwifery or medical treatment, or to carry off a dead body to the cremation or burial grounds, or those who go out with a lamp in hand at night, as well as those who go out to visit the officer in charge of the city, or to find out the cause of a trumpet sound (turyapreksha), or to extinguish the outbreak of fire or under the authority of a pass shall not be arrested.
AS-2.36.31.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 31 (AS-2.36.31)

AS-2.36.32.text: During the nights of free movement (chárarátrishu) those who move out under disguise, those who stir out though forbidden (pravarjitah), as well as those who move with clubs and other weapons in hand shall be punished in proportion to the gravity of their guilt.
AS-2.36.32.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 32 (AS-2.36.32)

AS-2.36.33.text: Those watchmen who stop whomever they ought not to stop, or do not stop whomever they ought to stop shall be punished with twice the amount of fine levied for untimely movement.
AS-2.36.33.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 33 (AS-2.36.33)

AS-2.36.34.text: When a watchman has carnal connection with a slave woman, he shall be punished with the first amercement; with a free woman middlemost amercement; with a woman arrested for untimely movement, the highest amercement; and a woman of high birth (kulastrí), he shall be put to death.
AS-2.36.34.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 34 (AS-2.36.34)

AS-2.36.35.text: When the officer in charge of the city (nágaraka) does not make a report (to the king) of whatever nocturnal nuisance of animate or inanimate nature (chetanâchetana) has occurred, or when he shows carelessness (in the discharge of his duty), he shall be punished in proportion to the gravity of his crime.
AS-2.36.35.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 35 (AS-2.36.35)

AS-2.36.36.text: He shall make a daily inspection of reservoirs of water, of roads, of the hidden passage for going out of the city, of forts, fortwalls, and other defensive works. He shall also keep in his safe custody of whatever things he comes across as lost, forgotten or left behind by others.
AS-2.36.36.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 36 (AS-2.36.36)

AS-2.36.37.text: On the days to which the birth star of the king is assigned, as well as on full moon days, such prisoners as are young, old, diseased, or helpless (anátha) shall be let out from the jail (bandhanâgâra); or those who are of charitable disposition or who have made any agreement with the prisoners may liberate them by paying an adequate ransom.
AS-2.36.37.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 37 (AS-2.36.37)

AS-2.36.38.text: Once in a day or once in five nights, jails may be emptied of prisoners in consideration of the work they have done, or of whipping inflicted upon them, or of an adequate ransom paid by them in gold.
AS-2.36.38.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 38 (AS-2.36.38)

AS-2.36.39.text: Whenever a new country is conquered, when an heir apparent is installed on the throne, or when a prince is born to the king, prisoners are usually set free.
AS-2.36.39.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 39 (AS-2.36.39)

AS-2.36.4.text: Managers of charitable institutions shall send information (to Gopa or Sthánika) as to any heretics (Páshanda) and travellers arriving to reside therein. They shall allow ascetics and men learned in the Vedas to reside in such places only when those persons are known to be of reliable character.
AS-2.36.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 4 (AS-2.36.4)

AS-2.36.5.text: Artisans and other handicraftsmen may, on their own responsibility, allow others of their own profession to reside where they carry on their own work (i.e., in their own houses).
AS-2.36.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 5 (AS-2.36.5)

AS-2.36.6.text: Similarly merchants may on their own responsibility allow other merchants to reside where they themselves carry on their mercantile work (i.e., their own houses or shops).
AS-2.36.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 6 (AS-2.36.6)

AS-2.36.7.text: They (the merchants) shall make a report of those who sell any merchandise in forbidden place or time, as well as of those who are in possession of any merchandise other than their own.
AS-2.36.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 7 (AS-2.36.7)

AS-2.36.8.text: Vintners, sellers of cooked flesh and cooked rice as well as prostitutes may allow any other person to reside with them only when that person is well-known to them.
AS-2.36.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 8 (AS-2.36.8)

AS-2.36.9.text: They (vintners, etc.) shall make a report of spendthrifts and fool-hardy persons who engage themselves in risky undertakings.
AS-2.36.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 36, Sutra 9 (AS-2.36.9)

AS-2.4.1.text: DEMARCATION of the ground inside the fort shall be made first by opening three royal roads from west to east and three from south to north.
AS-2.4.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 1 (AS-2.4.1)

AS-2.4.10.text: The treasury, the accountant’s office, and various manufactories (karmanishadyáscha) shall be situated on sites south by east.
AS-2.4.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 10 (AS-2.4.10)

AS-2.4.11.text: The store-house of forest produce and the arsenal shall be constructed on sites south by west.
AS-2.4.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 11 (AS-2.4.11)

AS-2.4.12.text: To the south, the superintendents of the city, of commerce, of manufactories, and of the army as well as those who trade in cooked rice, liquor, and flesh, besides prostitutes, musicians, and the people of Vaisya caste shall live.
AS-2.4.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 12 (AS-2.4.12)

AS-2.4.13.text: To the west by south, stables of asses, camels, and working house.
AS-2.4.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 13 (AS-2.4.13)

AS-2.4.14.text: To the west, artisans manufacturing worsted threads, cotton threads, bamboo-mats, skins, armours, weapons, and gloves as well as the people of Súdra caste shall have their dwellings.
AS-2.4.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 14 (AS-2.4.14)

AS-2.4.15.text: To the north by east, the treasury and the stables of cows and horses.
AS-2.4.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 15 (AS-2.4.15)

AS-2.4.16.text: To the north, the royal tutelary deity of the city, ironsmiths, artisans working on precious stones, as well as Bráhmans shall reside.
AS-2.4.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 16 (AS-2.4.16)

AS-2.4.17.text: In the several corners, guilds and corporations of workmen shall reside.
AS-2.4.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 17 (AS-2.4.17)

AS-2.4.18.text: In the centre of the city, the apartments of Gods such as Aparájita, Apratihata, Jayanta, Vaijayanta, Siva, Vaisravana, Asvina (divine physicians), and the honourable liquor-house (Srí-madiragriham), shall be situated.
AS-2.4.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 18 (AS-2.4.18)

AS-2.4.19.text: In the corners, the guardian deities of the ground shall be appropriately set up.
AS-2.4.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 19 (AS-2.4.19)

AS-2.4.2.text: The fort shall contain twelve gates, provided with both a land and water-way kept secret.
AS-2.4.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 2 (AS-2.4.2)

AS-2.4.20.text: Likewise the principal gates such as Bráhma, Aindra, Yámya, and Sainápatya shall be constructed; and at a distance of 100 bows (dhanus = 108 angulas) from the ditch (on the counterscarp side), places of worship and pilgrimage, groves and buildings shall be constructed.
AS-2.4.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 20 (AS-2.4.20)

AS-2.4.21.text: Guardian deities of all quarters shall also be set up in quarters appropriate to them.
AS-2.4.21.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 21 (AS-2.4.21)

AS-2.4.22.text: Either to the north or the east, burial or cremation grounds shall be situated; but that of the people of the highest caste shall be to the south (of the city).
AS-2.4.22.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 22 (AS-2.4.22)

AS-2.4.23.text: Violation of this rule shall be punished with the first amercement.
AS-2.4.23.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 23 (AS-2.4.23)

AS-2.4.24.text: Heretics and Chandálas shall live beyond the burial grounds.
AS-2.4.24.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 24 (AS-2.4.24)

AS-2.4.25.text: Families of workmen may in any other way be provided with sites befitting with their occupation and field work. Besides working in flower-gardens, fruit-gardens, vegetable-gardens, and paddy-fields allotted to them, they (families) shall collect grains and merchandise in abundance as authorised.
AS-2.4.25.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 25 (AS-2.4.25)

AS-2.4.26.text: Oils, grains, sugar, salt, medicinal articles, dry or fresh vegetables, meadow grass, dried flesh, haystock, firewood, metals, skins, charcoal, tendons (snáyu), poison, horns, bamboo, fibrous garments, strong timber, weapons, armour, and stones shall also be stored (in the fort) in such quantities as can be enjoyed for years together without feeling any want. Of such collection, old things shall be replaced by new ones when received.
AS-2.4.26.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 26 (AS-2.4.26)

AS-2.4.27.text: Elephants, cavalry, chariots, and infantry shall each be officered with many chiefs inasmuch as chiefs, when many, are under the fear of betrayal from each other and scarcely liable to the insinuations and intrigues of an enemy.
AS-2.4.27.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 27 (AS-2.4.27)

AS-2.4.28.text: The same rule shall hold good with the appointment of boundary, guards, and repairers of fortifications.
AS-2.4.28.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 28 (AS-2.4.28)

AS-2.4.29.text: Never shall báhirikas who are dangerous to the well being of cities and countries be kept in forts. They may either be thrown in country parts or compelled to pay taxes.
AS-2.4.29.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 29 (AS-2.4.29)

AS-2.4.3.text: Chariot-roads, royal roads, and roads leading to drónamukha, stháníya, country parts, and pasture grounds shall each be four dandas (24 ft.) in width.
AS-2.4.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 3 (AS-2.4.3)

AS-2.4.4.text: Roads leading to sayóníya (?), military stations (vyúha), burial or cremation grounds, and to villages shall be eight dandas in width.
AS-2.4.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 4 (AS-2.4.4)

AS-2.4.5.text: Roads for chariots shall be five aratnis (7½ ft.). Roads for cattle shall measure four aratnis; and roads for minor quadrupeds and men two aratnis.
AS-2.4.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 5 (AS-2.4.5)

AS-2.4.6.text: In the midst of the houses of the people of all the four castes and to the north from the centre of the ground inside the fort, the king’s palace, facing either the north or the east shall, as described elsewhere (Chapter XX, Book I), be constructed occupying one-ninth of the whole site inside the fort.
AS-2.4.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 6 (AS-2.4.6)

AS-2.4.7.text: Royal teachers, priests, sacrificial place, water-reservoir and ministers shall occupy sites east by north to the palace.
AS-2.4.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 7 (AS-2.4.7)

AS-2.4.8.text: Royal kitchen, elephant stables, and the store-house shall be situated on sites east by south.
AS-2.4.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 8 (AS-2.4.8)

AS-2.4.9.text: On the eastern side, merchants trading in scents, garlands, grains, and liquids, together with expert artisans and the people of Kshatriya caste shall have their habitations.
AS-2.4.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 4, Sutra 9 (AS-2.4.9)

AS-2.5.1.text: THE Chamberlain (sannidhátá = one who ever attends upon the king) shall see to the construction of the treasury-house, trading-house, the store-house of grains, the store-house of forest produce, the armoury and the jail.
AS-2.5.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 1 (AS-2.5.1)

AS-2.5.10.text: In (front of) the store-house a bowl (kunda) with its mouth as wide as an aratni (24 angulag) shall be set up as rain-gauge (varshamána).
AS-2.5.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 10 (AS-2.5.10)

AS-2.5.11.text: Assisted by experts having necessary qualifications and provided with tools and instruments, the chamberlain shall attend to the business of receiving gems either old or new, as well as raw materials of superior or inferior value.
AS-2.5.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 11 (AS-2.5.11)

AS-2.5.12.text: In cases of deception in gems, both the deceiver and the abettor shall be punished with the highest amercement; in the case of superior commodities, they shall be punished with the middle-most amercement; and in that of commodities of inferior value, they shall be compelled not only to restore the same, but also pay a fine equal to the value of the articles.
AS-2.5.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 12 (AS-2.5.12)

AS-2.5.13.text: He shall receive only such gold coins as have been declared to be pure by the examiner of coins.
AS-2.5.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 13 (AS-2.5.13)

AS-2.5.14.text: Whoever brings in counterfeit coins shall be punished with the first amercement.
AS-2.5.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 14 (AS-2.5.14)

AS-2.5.15.text: Grains pure and fresh shall be received in full measures; otherwise a fine of twice the value of the grains shall be imposed.
AS-2.5.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 15 (AS-2.5.15)

AS-2.5.16.text: The same rule shall hold good with the receipt of merchandise, raw materials, and weapons.
AS-2.5.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 16 (AS-2.5.16)

AS-2.5.17.text: In all departments, whoever, whether as an officer (yukta), a clerk (upayukta), or a servant (tatpurusha), misappropriates sums from one to four panas or any other valuable things shall be punished with the first, middlemost, and highest amercements and death respectively.
AS-2.5.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 17 (AS-2.5.17)

AS-2.5.18.text: If the officer who is in charge of the treasury causes loss in money, he shall be whipped (ghátah), while his abettors shall receive half the punishment; if the loss is due to ignorance, he shall be censured.
AS-2.5.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 18 (AS-2.5.18)

AS-2.5.19.text: If, with the intention of giving a hint, robbers are frightened (by the guards), (the latter) shall be tortured to death.
AS-2.5.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 19 (AS-2.5.19)

AS-2.5.2.text: Having dug up a square well not too deep to be moist with water, having paved both the bottom and the sides with slabs of stone, he shall, by using strong timber, construct in that well a cage-like under-ground chamber of three stories high, the top-most being on a level with the surface of the ground, with many compartments of various design, with floor plastered with small stones, with one door, with a movable staircase, and solemnised with the presence of the guardian deity.
AS-2.5.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 2 (AS-2.5.2)

AS-2.5.20.text: Hence assisted by trustworthy persons, the chamberlain shall attend to the business of revenue collection.
AS-2.5.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 20 (AS-2.5.20)

AS-2.5.21.text: He shall have so thorough a knowledge of both external and internal incomes running even for a hundred years that, when questioned, he can point out without hesitation the exact amount of net balance that remains after expenditure has been met with.
AS-2.5.21.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 21 (AS-2.5.21)

AS-2.5.3.text: Above this chamber, the treasury house closed on both sides, with projecting roofs and extensively opening into the store-house shall be built of bricks.
AS-2.5.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 3 (AS-2.5.3)

AS-2.5.4.text: He may employ outcast men (abhityakta-purusha) to build at the extreme boundary of the kingdom a palacious mansion to hold substantial treasure against dangers and calamities.
AS-2.5.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 4 (AS-2.5.4)

AS-2.5.5.text: The trading-house shall be a quadrangle enclosed by four buildings with one door, with pillars built of burnt bricks, with many compartments, and with a row of pillars on both sides kept apart.
AS-2.5.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 5 (AS-2.5.5)

AS-2.5.6.text: The store-house shall consist of many spacious rooms and enclose within itself the store-house of forest produce separated from it by means of wall and connected with both the underground chamber and the armoury.
AS-2.5.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 6 (AS-2.5.6)

AS-2.5.7.text: The court (dharmasthíya) and the office of the ministers (mahámátríya) shall be built in a separate locality.
AS-2.5.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 7 (AS-2.5.7)

AS-2.5.8.text: Provided with separate accommodation for men and women kept apart and with many compartments well guarded, a jail shall also be constructed.
AS-2.5.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 8 (AS-2.5.8)

AS-2.5.9.text: All these buildings shall be provided with halls (sála) pits (kháta—privy [?]), water-well, bath-room, remedies against fire and poison, with cats, mangooses, and with necessary means to worship the guardian gods appropriate to each.
AS-2.5.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 5, Sutra 9 (AS-2.5.9)

AS-2.6.1.text: THE Collector-General shall attend to (the collection of revenue from) forts (durga), country-parts (ráshtra), mines (khani), buildings and gardens (setu), forests (vana), herds of cattle (vraja), and roads of traffic (vanikpatha).
AS-2.6.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 1 (AS-2.6.1)

AS-2.6.10.text: The royal year, the month, the paksha, the day, the dawn (vyushta), the third and seventh pakshas of (the seasons such as) the rainy season, the winter season, and the summer short of their days, the rest complete, and a separate intercalary month are (the divisions of time).
AS-2.6.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 10 (AS-2.6.10)

AS-2.6.11.text: He shall also pay attention to the work in hand (karaníya), the work accomplished (siddham), part of a work in hand (sésha), receipts, expenditure, and net balance.
AS-2.6.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 11 (AS-2.6.11)

AS-2.6.12.text: The business of upkeeping the government (samsthánam), the routine work (prachárah), the collection of necessaries of life, the collection and audit of all kinds of revenue,—these constitute the work in hand.
AS-2.6.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 12 (AS-2.6.12)

AS-2.6.13.text: That which has been credited to the treasury; that which has been taken by the king; that which has been spent in connection with the capital city not entered (into the register) or continued from year before last, the royal command dictated or orally intimated to be entered (into the register),—all these constitute the work accomplished.
AS-2.6.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 13 (AS-2.6.13)

AS-2.6.14.text: Preparation of plans for profitable works, balance of fines due, demand for arrears of revenue kept in abeyance, and examination of accounts,—these constitute what is called part of a work in hand which may be of little or no value.
AS-2.6.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 14 (AS-2.6.14)

AS-2.6.15.text: Receipts may be (1) current, (2) last balance, and (3) accidental (anyajátah= received from external source).
AS-2.6.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 15 (AS-2.6.15)

AS-2.6.16.text: What is received day after day is termed current (vartamána).
AS-2.6.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 16 (AS-2.6.16)

AS-2.6.17.text: Whatever has been brought forward from year before last, whatever is in the hands of others, and whatever has changed hands is termed last balance (puryushita).
AS-2.6.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 17 (AS-2.6.17)

AS-2.6.18.text: Whatever has been lost and forgotten (by others), fines levied from government servants, marginal revenue (pársva), compensation levied for any damage (párihínikam), presentations to the king, the property of those who have fallen victims to epidemics (damaragatakasvam) leaving no sons, and treasure-troves,---all these constitute accidental receipts.
AS-2.6.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 18 (AS-2.6.18)

AS-2.6.19.text: Investment of capital (vikshépa), the relics of a wrecked undertaking, and the savings from an estimated outlay are the means to check expenditure (vyayapratyayah).
AS-2.6.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 19 (AS-2.6.19)

AS-2.6.2.text: Tolls, fines, weights and measures, the town-clerk (nágaraka), the superintendent of coinage (lakshanádhyakshah), the superintendent of seals and pass-ports, liquor, slaughter of animals, threads, oils,. ghee, sugar (kshára), the state-goldsmith (sauvarnika), the warehouse of merchandise, the prostitute, gambling, building sites (vástuka), the corporation of artisans and handicrafts-men (kárusilpiganah), the superintendent of gods, and taxes collected at the gates and from the people (known as) Báhirikas come under the head of forts.
AS-2.6.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 2 (AS-2.6.2)

AS-2.6.20.text: The rise in price of merchandise due to the use of different weights and measures in selling is termed vyáji; the enhancement of price due to bidding among buyers is also another source of profit.
AS-2.6.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 20 (AS-2.6.20)

AS-2.6.21.text: Expenditure is of two kinds—daily expenditure and profitable expenditure.
AS-2.6.21.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 21 (AS-2.6.21)

AS-2.6.22.text: Whatever is earned once in a paksha, a month, or a year is termed profit.
AS-2.6.22.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 22 (AS-2.6.22)

AS-2.6.23.text: Whatever is spent on these two heads is termed as daily expenditure and profitable expenditure respectively.
AS-2.6.23.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 23 (AS-2.6.23)

AS-2.6.24.text: That which remains after deducting all the expenditure already incurred and excluding all revenue to be realised is net balance (nívi) which may have been either just realised or brought forward.
AS-2.6.24.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 24 (AS-2.6.24)

AS-2.6.25.text: Thus a wise collector-general shall conduct the work of revenue-collection, increasing the income and decreasing the expenditure.
AS-2.6.25.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 25 (AS-2.6.25)

AS-2.6.3.text: Produce from crown-lands (sita), portion of produce payable to the government (bhága), religious taxes (bali), taxes paid in money (kara), merchants, the superintendent of rivers, ferries, boats, and ships, towns, pasture grounds, road-cess (vartani), ropes (rajjú) and ropes to bind thieves (chórarajjú) come under the head of country parts.
AS-2.6.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 3 (AS-2.6.3)

AS-2.6.4.text: Gold, silver, diamonds, gems, pearls, corals, conch-shells, metals (loha), salt, and other minerals extracted from plains and mountain slopes come under the head of mines.
AS-2.6.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 4 (AS-2.6.4)

AS-2.6.5.text: Flower-gardens, fruit-gardens, vegetable-gardens, wet fields, and fields where crops are grown by sowing roots for seeds (múlavápáh, i.e., sugar-cane crops, etc.) come under sétu.
AS-2.6.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 5 (AS-2.6.5)

AS-2.6.6.text: Game-forests, timber-forests, and elephant-forests are forests.
AS-2.6.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 6 (AS-2.6.6)

AS-2.6.7.text: Cows, buffaloes, goats, sheep, asses, camels, horses, and mules come under the head of herds.
AS-2.6.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 7 (AS-2.6.7)

AS-2.6.8.text: Capital (múla), share (bhága), premia (vyáji), parigha (?) fixed taxes (klripta), premia on coins (rúpika), and fixed fines (atyaya) are the several forms of revenue (áyamukha, i.e., the mouth from which income is to issue).
AS-2.6.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 8 (AS-2.6.8)

AS-2.6.9.text: The chanting of auspicious hymns during the worship of gods and ancestors, and on the occasion of giving gifts, the harem, the kitchen, the establishment of messengers, the store-house, the armoury, the warehouse, the store-house of raw materials, manufactories (karmánta), free labourers (vishti), maintenance of infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants, herds of cows, the museum of beasts, deer, birds, and snakes, and storage of firewood and fodder constitute the body of expenditure (vyayasaríram).
AS-2.6.9.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 6, Sutra 9 (AS-2.6.9)

AS-2.7.1.text: THE superintendent of accounts shall have the accountant's office constructed with its door facing either the north or the east, with seats (for clerks) kept apart and with shelves of account-books well arranged.
AS-2.7.1.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 1 (AS-2.7.1)

AS-2.7.10.text: The school of Manu hold that a fine equal to the loss of revenue and multiplied by the serial number of the circumstances of the guilt just narrated in order shall be imposed upon him.
AS-2.7.10.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 10 (AS-2.7.10)

AS-2.7.11.text: The school of Parásara hold that the fine in all the cases shall be eight times the amount lost.
AS-2.7.11.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 11 (AS-2.7.11)

AS-2.7.12.text: The school of Brihaspathi say that it shall be ten times the amount.
AS-2.7.12.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 12 (AS-2.7.12)

AS-2.7.13.text: The school of Usanas say that it shall be twenty times the amount.
AS-2.7.13.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 13 (AS-2.7.13)

AS-2.7.14.text: But Kautilya says that it shall be proportional to the guilt.
AS-2.7.14.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 14 (AS-2.7.14)

AS-2.7.15.text: When they (the accountants of different districts) present themselves with sealed books, commodities and net revenue, they shall all be kept apart in one place so that they cannot carry on conversation with each other. Having heard from them the totals of receipts, expenditure, and net revenue, the net amount shall be received.
AS-2.7.15.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 15 (AS-2.7.15)

AS-2.7.16.text: By how much the superintendent of a department augments the net total of its revenue either by increasing any one of the items of its receipts or by decreasing anyone of the items of expenditure, he shall be rewarded eight times that amount. But when it is reversed (i.e., when the net total is decreased), the award shall also be reversed (i.e., he shall be made to pay eight times the decrease).
AS-2.7.16.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 16 (AS-2.7.16)

AS-2.7.17.text: Those accountants who do not present themselves in time or do not produce their account books along with the net revenue shall be fined ten times the amount due from them.
AS-2.7.17.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 17 (AS-2.7.17)

AS-2.7.18.text: When a superintendent of accounts (káranika) does not at once proceed to receive and check the accounts when the clerks (kármika) are ready, he shall be punished with the first amercement. In the reverse case (i.e., when the clerks are not ready), the clerks shall be punished with double the first amercement.
AS-2.7.18.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 18 (AS-2.7.18)

AS-2.7.19.text: All the ministers (mahámáras) shall together narrate the whole of the actual accounts pertaining to each department.
AS-2.7.19.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 19 (AS-2.7.19)

AS-2.7.2.text: Therein the number of several departments; the description of the work carried on and of the results realised in several manufactories (Karmánta); the amount of profit, loss, expenditure, delayed earnings, the amount of vyáji (premia in kind or cash) realised,—the status of government agency employed, the amount of wages paid, the number of free labourers engaged (vishti) pertaining to the investment of capital on any work; likewise in the case of gems and commodities of superior or inferior value, the rate of their price, the rate of their barter, the counterweights (pratimána) used in weighing them, their number, their weight, and their cubical measure; the history of customs, professions, and transactions of countries, villages, families, and corporations;
AS-2.7.2.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 2 (AS-2.7.2)

AS-2.7.20.text: Whoever of these (ministers or clerks ?) is of undivided counsel or keeps himself aloof, or utters falsehood shall be punished with the highest amercement.
AS-2.7.20.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 20 (AS-2.7.20)

AS-2.7.21.text: When an accountant has not prepared the table of daily accounts (akritáhorúpaharam), he may be given a month more (for its preparation). After the lapse of one month he shall be fined at the rate of 200 panas for each month (during which he delays the accounts).
AS-2.7.21.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 21 (AS-2.7.21)

AS-2.7.22.text: If an accountant has to write only a small portion of the accounts pertaining to net revenue, he may be allowed five nights to prepare it.
AS-2.7.22.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 22 (AS-2.7.22)

AS-2.7.23.text: Then the table of daily accounts submitted by him along with the net revenue shall be checked with reference to the regulated forms of righteous transactions and precedents and by applying such arithmetical processes as addition, subtraction, inference and by espionage. It shall also be verified with reference to (such divisions of time as) days, five nights, pakshás, months, four-months, and the year.
AS-2.7.23.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 23 (AS-2.7.23)

AS-2.7.24.text: The receipt shall be verified with reference to the place and time pertaining to them, the form of their collection (i.e., capital, share), the amount of the present and past produce, the person who has paid it, the person who caused its payment, the officer who fixed the amount payable, and the officer who received it. The expenditure shall be verified with reference to the cause of the profit from any source in the place and time pertaining to each item, the amount payable, the amount paid, the person who ordered the collection, the person who remitted the same, the person who delivered it, and the person who finally received it.
AS-2.7.24.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 24 (AS-2.7.24)

AS-2.7.25.text: Likewise the net revenue shall be verified with reference to the place, time, and source pertaining to it, its standard of fineness and quantity, and the persons who are employed to guard the deposits and magazines (of grains, etc.).
AS-2.7.25.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 25 (AS-2.7.25)

AS-2.7.26.text: When an officer (káranika) does not facilitate or prevents the execution of the king's order, or renders the receipts and expenditure otherwise than prescribed, he shall be punished with the first amercement.
AS-2.7.26.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 26 (AS-2.7.26)

AS-2.7.27.text: Any clerk who violates or deviates from the prescribed form of writing accounts, enters what is unknown to him, or makes double or treble entries (punaruktam) shall be fined 12 panas.
AS-2.7.27.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 27 (AS-2.7.27)

AS-2.7.28.text: He who causes loss of revenue shall not only pay a fine equal to five times the amount lost (panchabandha), but also make good the loss. In case of uttering a lie, the punishment levied for theft shall be imposed. (When an entry lost or omitted) is made later or is made to appear as forgotten, but added later on recollection, the punishment shall be double the above.
AS-2.7.28.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 28 (AS-2.7.28)

AS-2.7.29.text: The king shall forgive an offence when it is trifling, have satisfaction even when the revenue is scanty, and honour with rewards (pragraha) such of his superintendents as are of immense benefit to him.
AS-2.7.29.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 29 (AS-2.7.29)

AS-2.7.3.text: the gains in the form of gifts to the king's courtiers, their title to possess and enjoy lands, remission of taxes allowed to them, and payment of provisions and salaries to them; the gains to the wives and sons of the king in gems, lands, prerogatives, and provisions made to remedy evil portents; the treaties with, issues of ultimatum to, and payments of tribute from or to, friendly or inimical kings,— all these shall be regularly entered in prescribed registers.
AS-2.7.3.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 3 (AS-2.7.3)

AS-2.7.4.text: From these books the superintendent shall furnish the accounts as to the forms of work in hand, of works accomplished, of part of works in hand, of receipts, of expenditure, of net balance, and of tasks to be undertaken in each of the several departments.
AS-2.7.4.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 4 (AS-2.7.4)

AS-2.7.5.text: To supervise works of high, middling and low description, superintendents with corresponding qualifications shall be employed.
AS-2.7.5.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 5 (AS-2.7.5)

AS-2.7.6.text: The king will have to suffer in the end if he curtails the fixed amount of expenditure on profitable works.
AS-2.7.6.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 6 (AS-2.7.6)

AS-2.7.7.text: (When a man engaged by Government for any work absents himself), his sureties who conjointly received (wages?) from the government, or his sons, brothers, wives, daughters or servants living upon his work shall bear the loss caused to the Government.
AS-2.7.7.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 7 (AS-2.7.7)

AS-2.7.8.text: The work of 354 days and nights is a year. Such a work shall be paid for more or less in proportion to its quantity at the end of the month, Ashádha (about the middle of July). (The work during) the intercalary month shall be (separately) calculated.
AS-2.7.8.label: Arthashastra Book 2, Chapter 7, Sutra 8 (AS-2.7.8)
